title: Sharadar SFP adjusted-close spikes
statement: closeadj has one-day spikes that reverse the next day (191 cases in 67 funds 1998-2026, e.g. SSO 2014-06-24 x3.95), split adjustments applied to a single day. The SFP loader drops those days (data.drop_spikes, |log move| > 0.4 reversed within 0.1).

title: DefiLlama stablecoin history is recomputed
statement: The DefiLlama stablecoin endpoint recomputes the whole history on every call and adds coins and chains retroactively, so past values are not what was visible at the time. Any signal on it carries look-ahead in levels and growth rates, worst in 2018-2020.

title: Single stocks fit in RAM only up to LIQ-500
statement: The LIQ-1000 panel has 4 581 stocks; a card on LIQ-500 or the S&P 500 loads ~2 400 columns (float32) and peaks at 1.7-2.4 GB in G2 on this 3.9 GB machine. LIQ-1000 does not fit.

title: No earnings dates in the lab
statement: Sharadar SF1 filing dates exist on disk but there is no loader, and announcement dates are not in any loadable dataset. Earnings-event ideas can only use proxies (volume seasonality), which H-0008 showed to be weak.

title: Benchmark-relative binary switches start handicapped
statement: A strategy that moves the whole book between two assets on a state variable carries a different average exposure than the constant-mix benchmark; it must beat the benchmark's risk-adjusted return with less diversification. Test the state variable as a tilt around the benchmark weights, or against a control with the same average exposure.

title: Short dev windows cannot confirm crypto ideas
statement: Crypto dev data ends 2022-12-31 and starts 2017-2020 depending on the dataset, so weekly strategies have few independent decisions; point estimates can beat BTC while the bootstrap bound stays below zero. Prefer daily decisions or many instruments, and treat a near miss as 'cannot tell', not as evidence.

title: Run the mechanism diagnostic before the strategy
statement: Three cards died at G1 before their own mechanism checks could run. An event study or conditional-return diagnostic of the mechanism (with a placebo) is cheaper and more informative than a full strategy when the mechanism itself is uncertain. Diagnostics on dev data are trials too and must be counted.

title: Gate runner fixes found by real hypotheses
statement: Real runs exposed judge bugs that the canaries did not: a per-period bootstrap bound reported next to annualized Sharpe (H-0001), two requirements on one dataset overwriting each other (H-0003), generic series filtered by the card's guessed field names (H-0005), spot+perp cards getting the cross-asset benchmark (H-0006), a random-entry null drawn from illiquid stocks (H-0007). Every fix re-ran the canaries; affected verdicts were voided only when the bug changed them.

title: G0 look-ahead tests are weak on sparse decisions
statement: Truncation and perturbation at random rows rarely hit the decision rows of weekly or monthly strategies, and rank-based weights often do not change under perturbation. G0 now also cuts on rows where the weights change; the Skeptic must still read the code of sparse strategies.

title: Fail loudly on missing inputs
statement: A strategy that silently holds nothing when a series or instrument is missing passes G0 and dies at G1 for the wrong reason (H-0005, first run). Builders index inputs directly so a missing one raises.

title: Scouts converge without a brief
statement: Without steering, three of the first four cards used SPY/IEF and monthly switching. Rotating briefs (least-used horizon x asset group, multi-timeframe while under half of the cards combine timeframes) produced three different markets and horizons in the next three runs.

title: US stock intraday-return reversal is fragile
statement: A weekly long/short on intraday-return reversal in LIQ-500 beat T-bills in dev on the point estimate and against random entries, but not in the S&P 500 universe, with most of the return in the earliest era and a peaked parameter choice, the same pattern as research 5.

title: Paper trading is model execution on forward data
statement: The lab places no orders. Paper = the strategy run by the lab engine on daily bars that did not exist when it was judged, appended once per day and never recomputed. It is clean out-of-sample evidence for the signal and the cost model's assumptions, not for real fills or slippage; G5 therefore cannot test tracking or realized costs.

title: Only crypto has forward data
statement: Forward daily bars come from the Binance public API (spot and USD-M perps with funding), reachable from this VPS. ETFs and US stocks have no free forward source yet (Sharadar not renewed), so hypotheses on them are parked after G4 until the Archivist validates a source.

title: systemd hardening can silently break the agent user switch
statement: ProtectKernelTunables, ProtectKernelModules, LockPersonality (and other options) imply NoNewPrivileges, which makes sudo refuse to switch to labagent. The first production cycles failed this way; the unit now omits them, and three agent runs failing before any model turn pause the lab with a critical alert instead of retrying every 30 minutes.

title: A deny rule meant for the lab state blinded the agents
statement: The agents' settings denied Read(//srv/**) to protect the lab state; in production the workspaces live under /srv/research-lab/workspaces, so every file tool was denied and two Scout runs produced nothing. Deny rules must name the protected directories exactly; a test now checks that none covers a workspace. The Scouts reported the problem as owner questions instead of improvising, which is the intended behaviour.

title: The random-entry null was survivorship-biased
statement: G2's random-entry null drew random stocks from those listed in more than half of the dev window, a pool chosen with knowledge of who lasted. Its median Sharpe (0.62) beat both the market (0.36) and a real low-volatility book, so no long-only stock strategy could pass. Found by calibrating on real data. The null is now built date by date from the instruments eligible on that date, with the real book's retention so that turnover matches.

title: Position-entry minimum rejected always-invested books
statement: min_position_entries counted only flat-to-position entries: a delta-neutral funding carry has 4 entries but 156 weekly rebalances and was rejected at G1 despite a Sharpe of 8.4. For books invested at least half the time the rebalancing dates now count as bets (gates.yaml continuous_min_exposure).

title: The judge was calibrated against five known strategies
statement: Low-vol stocks, funding carry, 12-1 momentum, 5-day reversal and a BTC trend filter were run through the real gates in a throwaway lab (lab calibrate). Verdicts agree with the owner's earlier studies: nothing passes unexplained, low-vol reaches G2 and dies on publication decay, carry dies on sub-period concentration, the rest die at G1. This shows the judge is not lenient; it cannot show that it passes a genuinely good real strategy because none is known.

title: Spot catalog range was longer than the loadable data
statement: The catalog said Binance spot daily data runs to 2026-10-03 but the research 9 panel the loader reads ends 2026-08-31; the gate runner takes the end of a card's data from the catalog range, so perp-plus-spot cards would have run on a month of missing spot rows. The range now says 2026-08-31.

title: Mechanism tests before strategies
statement: Cards can declare an event and a horizon; the judge runs an event study against time-shifted placebos on dev rows before simulating the strategy. A strategy whose claimed mechanism is absent dies at G1 with a mechanism reason, which separates 'the idea is wrong' from 'this strategy was too weak'. It counts as one trial of the family. Placebo percentile is the gate, not a t-statistic.

title: First production mechanism tests killed two ideas without a strategy run
statement: Two of the first cards with a mechanism test (ex-dividend price pressure, breakouts through stale 52-week highs, both LIQ-500 market-neutral, 5-day horizon) died at G1 on the event study: placebo percentiles 0.64 and 0.46, gross abnormal return per event covering only 4 % and 28 % of the round-trip cost. The strategy was never simulated, so each death cost a Scout run and a Builder run but no gate time, and the reason is mechanism-level, not 'the strategy lost to the benchmark'.

title: Attached stock datasets fit in RAM with at most six fields
statement: SF1, insider and 13F fields are daily float32 matrices on the SEP stocks, 70 MB each. A LIQ-500 card with six fields peaks at 2.3 GB through G0-G2 on this machine (limit 2.8 GB for the cycle), three fields at 2.1 GB, so the per-card cap is six. Loading them takes seconds to a minute; fundamentals change only on filings, so signals built from them are slow.

title: Large-cap short-horizon event anomalies vanish; mandated-flow events survive
statement: Five-session event studies on documented US single-stock anomalies (ex-dividend run-up, stale 52-week-high breakouts, insider purchase filings, correlated-peer catch-up, abnormal volume, predicted earnings dates) found nothing distinguishable from time-shifted placebos among the most liquid stocks, and gross effects were far below spread cost. The only two events with an effect that cleared or nearly cleared the placebo bar were driven by mandated flows rather than information or sentiment: the month-turn beta spread and index inclusion. Together with K-0012 this suggests the large-cap short-horizon cross-section is efficient at this cost level, and the remaining candidates are flow events.

title: Read the placebo average, not the raw abnormal return
statement: The placebo keeps the same stocks and shifts the dates, so it absorbs any drift that belongs to the stock selection (names with a clean earnings spike, stocks at 52-week highs). In H-0011 and H-0015 the raw abnormal return was positive and still no better than the placebo average. Cards and lessons should judge an event set against the placebo average and spread, and a positive gross number alone is not evidence of a mechanism. Event-matched controls (same prior return, size or distance to the high) would separate selection from timing.

title: The placebo gate has little power for sparse event sets
statement: With a few hundred events on a few hundred dates the placebo distribution is wide, and a real effect that exceeds costs several times can still land just under the percentile bar (H-0017, which also lost a few placebo runs). The gate is a fixed threshold, not a statistic, so the verdict stands, but a Scout who wants to test a sparse event should widen the event set (more occurrences, both directions) instead of tweaking hold or filters on the same events, which would be counted as new trials of the same data. Reading near misses as a coin flip is more honest than reading them as promising.

title: A passing mechanism test does not make a tradable stand-alone window book
statement: H-0016 is the first card whose event study cleared the placebo bar and was then simulated as a strategy: the month-turn beta spread exists but the book is invested about a fifth of the days, so its Sharpe is capped by the window's own Sharpe and it missed the absolute bar and the bootstrap bound against T-bills. Calendar windows should be tested as a tilt on an always-invested benchmark with the same average exposure (see K-0005), or combined into one overlay, not as flat-otherwise books against cash. The mechanism gate and the strategy gate answer different questions and should be read separately.

title: G0 checks are vacuous when the synthetic market lacks the card's data, and card diagnostics cannot be reported
statement: Three of eight cards in this batch had a G0 look-ahead check that exercised nothing on the synthetic market: no dividends (H-0010), no insider events (H-0012), and only 80 names so the book never traded (H-0013). The Builders substituted hand-made tests, which no gate reads. Separately, two cards promised sanity diagnostics (regular-payer share in H-0010, volume hit rate of the predicted earnings days in H-0015) that the Builders could not output because no channel to the gate result exists, so a failed proxy cannot be told from an absent effect. Extend the synthetic market or the diagnostic output, and the Skeptic should read the code of data-specific cards.

title: The engine cannot hold stocks that have left the declared universe, so exit-from-universe events are untestable
statement: A card on the sp500 universe that must hold a stock after its removal from the index fails at G0 with g0_outside_universe: weights on non-members are refused. H-0018 (deletion leg of the index-change reversal) stalled this way, the Builder reported it in six of seven runs, and the card was parked by the owner at DATA_READY without ever becoming a trial. Any card whose key leg sits outside its own universe definition (deleted index members, names dropped from LIQ-500 after the event) has the same problem. The Scout's self-declared risk and the Builder's loud failure worked as intended, but the lab still paid several Builder runs before a human parked it.

title: A passing mechanism test is necessary, not sufficient: pooled events hide era fade, clustering and re-weighting costs
statement: Two cards now cleared the event-study gate and then failed the strategy gate with a net return close to cash: H-0016 (month-turn beta spread) and H-0019 (post-filing net-flow spread, the clearest pass so far). The pooled mean abnormal return per event overstates what a book earns because (1) the effect faded across sub-periods in both cases and the latest third is the one that predicts the future; (2) events cluster in a few weeks, so the book is invested a fraction of the time with small weights per name; (3) the strategy's daily re-equalising of weights adds turnover that the per-event round-trip cost ratio leaves out. Before filing a strategy on a passed mechanism, check the latest sub-period alone against cost, estimate the book's annual gross as events times weight times effect, and prefer a low-turnover tilt on an always-invested benchmark. Extends K-0027 from calendar windows to any clustered event set.

title: Compare the placebo bar with the round-trip cost to tell a power problem from an untradable effect
statement: A mechanism failure at G1 is a 'cannot tell' only when the placebo bar (its upper percentile) lies above the round-trip cost, because then a tradable effect could still have missed it (H-0017, sparse events). When the bar lies below the cost, as in H-0020 with a very large event count and a narrow placebo cloud, any effect worth trading would have cleared it, so the failure means the effect is not tradable in that form. Event counts alone mislead: events within a date share one cross-section, so what matters is the width of the placebo cloud, which the gate result reports. This refines K-0026: widening the event set helps only if it narrows the cloud below the cost.

title: Events on young or departing stocks, or needing index membership, do not fit the point-in-time universes
statement: Three cards in two families hit the same wall in different forms. H-0018 (deleted index members) failed at G0 because weights outside the S&P 500 universe are refused. H-0021 (IPO lockup expiry in LIQ-500) found zero events across the whole dev period, so G1 rejected it on the event count with no mechanism result; recent IPOs apparently never sit in the liquid universe at the event date (cause not confirmed). H-0022 (S&P changes read inside LIQ-500) was parked by the owner because the PIT S&P 500 mask is not available to liq_n cards, although the catalog lists alt_universe among the sharadar_sep extras. None produced evidence about its mechanism. Before a Builder run, a Scout should check that the event subject can be a member of the declared universe at the event date and that every input is delivered for that universe kind; a cheap event-count feasibility check would save runs.

title: G0 look-ahead checks are vacuous for event cards, and diagnostics cannot be reported (now five cards)
statement: Five event cards since H-0010 had a G0 look-ahead check that exercised nothing: no dividends (H-0010), no insider events (H-0012), too few names for the book to trade (H-0013), and now constant dollar volume on the synthetic market (H-0024) and no lockup events (H-0021). Builders substituted hand-made tests, which no gate reads. Two cards also promised sanity diagnostics (regular-payer share in H-0010, volume hit rate in H-0015) that had no channel to the gate result; H-0024 has the same open question about whether its volume-spike filter finds release days. Extend the synthetic market with the data the card needs (volume spikes, dividends, filings, listings) and add a diagnostic output channel; until then the Skeptic should read the event code of data-specific cards.

title: Compare the placebo bar with the round-trip cost: many events can still leave a bar above cost
statement: A mechanism failure at G1 is a 'cannot tell' when the placebo bar (its upper percentile) lies above the round-trip cost, because a tradable effect could still miss it. H-0017 (sparse events) and now H-0024 (thousands of events on over a thousand dates) are such cases: right sign, gross above cost, percentile just under the bar, bar above cost. Event count does not cure it, because events within a date share one cross-section and earnings seasons cluster dates. When the bar lies below cost (H-0020) the failure means the effect is not tradable in that form. Widening the event set helps only if it narrows the cloud below the cost; tuning filters or horizon on the same events creates new trials. Read near misses as a coin flip, not as promise.

title: Real earnings-release dates now exist (sec_8k_item202), from late 2004 and with coverage gaps
statement: The EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 flag (ea_reaction_day) replaces the volume proxies of H-0008 and H-0015 and was used first by H-0023. It starts with the August 2004 reform, so predicted dates (last year plus 52 weeks) exist from 2005; the 1998-2004 part of dev has no earnings events. The catalog quality line shows filings for only 10 218 of 17 958 CIKs, and the known biases say that CIKs EDGAR no longer serves and releases filed under other items are missed. Firms that delisted are the likely gaps, so event sets built on it may lean toward survivors; no one has measured how far. The dataset has no hit-rate output either: whether a rule such as 'last year plus 52 weeks' finds the actual release day was a declared diagnostic of H-0023 that never reached the gate result (see K-0033). Treat the dataset as usable but unvalidated for coverage in point-in-time liquid universes.

title: G0 look-ahead checks are vacuous for event cards, and diagnostics cannot be reported (now seven cards)
statement: Seven event or window cards since H-0010 had a G0 look-ahead check that exercised little or nothing: no dividends (H-0010), no insider events (H-0012), too few names for the book to trade (H-0013), constant dollar volume (H-0024), no lockup events (H-0021), and now only two events for H-0023's earnings dates and a single event date for H-0025's month-turn switches on the synthetic market. Builders substituted hand-made tests (a random quarterly-filing market in H-0023), which no gate reads. Declared diagnostics also have no channel to the gate result: regular-payer share (H-0010), volume hit rate (H-0015, H-0024), date-prediction hit rate (H-0023), and the switch A/B split and the static low-beta control (H-0025). Two of these are the very thing that decides whether a negative is about the idea or the proxy. Extend the synthetic market with the data the card needs (volume spikes, dividends, filings, listings, filing flags per quarter) and add a diagnostic output channel; until then the Skeptic should read the event code of data-specific cards, and Scouts should not rely on a declared diagnostic being reported.

title: Earnings-announcement premium: absent as a tradable effect in large liquid US stocks, with real dates too
statement: Three tries now cover the premium around scheduled earnings releases in the liquid US universe: two with volume-based date proxies, whose failure could not be attributed, and one with real release dates from filings, which removes that excuse. With real dates the event set was large and spread over the whole sample, the sign was positive and not fading, but the effect was indistinguishable from placebo windows of the same stocks and smaller than the cost of trading it with a five-session window and weekly-scale rotation. The literature premium probably lives in less covered stocks or in the release session itself, neither of which the five-session LIQ-500 design can see. This supports K-0024 (short-horizon information and sentiment events in large caps are gone), now for dated earnings events. Date-based earnings ideas on other mechanisms (surprise, timing changes) are separate claims.

title: The month-turn high-beta advantage passes the placebo test but fades in the later years
statement: Two designs on the same month-turn window in liquid US stocks (a high-minus-low beta spread, and a long-only rotation between a high-beta and a low-beta quintile) both cleared the mechanism test against time-shifted placebos, and in both the effect was strongest in the earliest third of the sample and weakest in the latest, in the rotation reversing sign. The two cards share events and data, so this is one piece of evidence seen twice, not two confirmations. It fits a published flow effect that is being arbitraged away, or a beta payoff that depends on the bull-market era. The rotation also gave no drawdown protection relative to the market. A month-turn beta claim should be expected to fail sub-period and publication-decay checks unless a new design shows the latest years separately.

title: Large-cap earnings-date events fail the placebo test: premium, surprise, delay
statement: Real release dates now support three claims in liquid US stocks over a five-session window: a long premium around the predicted date (H-0023), surprise drift at concurrent filings (H-0024) and a short on late releases (H-0026). None cleared the placebo bar. Surprise drift is a near miss whose bar lies above cost, so it is a 'cannot tell'; the delay signal has a bar below cost and reversed sign in the latest third, so it is not tradable in this form. Large-cap releases are pre-announced and heavily covered, so timing and surprise are likely priced quickly. With K-0024, further date-based earnings cards in this universe have a low prior unless they change the horizon to the release session, the stocks to less-covered names, or the data to announced dates.

title: G0 look-ahead checks are vacuous for event cards; diagnostics cannot be reported (eight cards)
statement: Eight event or window cards since H-0010 had a G0 look-ahead check that exercised little or nothing on the synthetic market: no dividends (H-0010), no insider events (H-0012), too few names (H-0013), constant volume (H-0024), no lockups (H-0021), two events (H-0023), one event date (H-0025), and now H-0026, whose synthetic filing flags cannot produce an overdue event although the real dev set had thousands. Builders substitute hand-made tests that no gate reads. Declared diagnostics have no channel to the gate result (payer share, volume and date hit rates, switch split, static control, overdue-rule hit rate). Extend the synthetic market with the data each card needs and add a diagnostic output channel; until then the Skeptic should read the event code, and Scouts should not count on a declared diagnostic being reported.

title: The trading-window net-flow spread does not survive a move from the filing date to the real release date
statement: The net-repurchaser-minus-stock-compensation-supplier spread in liquid US stocks passed the event-study gate clearly when anchored to the quarterly filing (H-0019) but fell short of the placebo bar when anchored to the real earnings release (H-0027), where it also built slowly with the horizon, had nothing in the first sessions and reversed sign in the latest third. A flow concentrated just after the trading window opens would show up at the release anchor and early horizons; it did not. The filing-anchored result is better read as filing-linked news or earnings-season drift, or as a slow style difference between repurchasers and issuers that the placebo (same stocks) cannot net out. Treat the trading-window flow family as closed for five-session books in LIQ-500; any remaining claim is a slow tilt, to be argued as a style premium.

title: A passing mechanism test can still end in a book below cash, even without fade
statement: Three cards now cleared the event-study gate and then failed the strategy gate: H-0016, H-0019 and H-0028. The first two had an explanation in K-0030 (era fade, clustered events, thin exposure). H-0028 has none of them: the effect cleared the placebo bar by a wide margin, covered cost, was positive in every third including the latest, and the book was invested about half the time, yet its net Sharpe was below T-bills with a deep drawdown for a market-neutral book. The remaining suspects are differences between the study and the book: event weights shrink when many names report on the same day (the study weights events equally), the equal-weight hedge basket adds turnover and cost, a generic cost tier for names that just moved several standard deviations, and short-side squeezes. The gate output has no gross-versus-net split or event-weighted study, so these cannot be separated. Until it does, a mechanism pass should be read as 'the signal exists in an equal-weight event study', and a Scout should estimate the book's gross (events per year times the weight per event times the effect) and its hedge turnover before filing a strategy.

title: The market's own release-session reaction predicts same-direction returns in liquid stocks
statement: On real earnings-release dates in liquid US stocks after 2004, stocks with a large standardized reaction on the release session had abnormal returns in the same direction over the next sessions that were clearly distinguishable from time-shifted placebos of the same stocks, positive in every third of the sample including the latest, and mostly concentrated in the first sessions after entry. The earlier test that used the accounting earnings change at the filing date as the surprise (H-0024) was only a near miss. This qualifies K-0039, which expected that large-cap surprise is priced quickly: a price-based surprise measure at the release session behaves differently from an accounting-based one at the filing. It is a single trial, and the long/short book built on it lost to T-bills, so tradability is not established and the cause of the gap is open (see the method entry on mechanism-versus-book gaps).

title: Weekly return-sort effects in the most liquid US stocks are smaller than cost, in either sign
statement: Past-month-return effects in liquid US stocks have now been tested with a reversal sign (H-0007, K-0012), with a conditional continuation sign (H-0029, highest-turnover stocks) and with a reversal sign after removing earnings sessions and adjusting for correlated peers in the S&P 500 (H-0030). None gave a tradable five-session effect: H-0029 was inside the placebo cloud with a bar below cost and a negative latest third, H-0030 cleared the placebo bar but earned well under round-trip cost, and H-0007 was early-era and small-name. Conditioning the sort (news, turnover, intraday split, peers) changes the sign or the significance, not the order of magnitude relative to cost. A further conditioner on the same one-month sort in the large-cap universe has a low prior; a cost-light implementation or a less-covered universe would be a different claim.

title: G0 look-ahead checks stay vacuous for cards with minimum-size rules (now eleven cards)
statement: Four more cards passed G0 without the look-ahead check exercising the signal: H-0027 (synthetic market has fewer names than the 100-name minimum, so zero events and zero positions), H-0028 (no release flag is ever set), H-0029 (legs never reach the five-name minimum; a temporary run with the minimum lowered traded and passed) and H-0030 (release flag filled with arbitrary floats; the Builder changed the test to make it bite). The problem is therefore not limited to event cards: any minimum-count rule above the size of the 80-name synthetic market has the same effect. Builders again wrote hand-made tests that no gate reads. In addition, cases.json shows no Skeptic message for H-0027 to H-0030 although each Builder summary asked the Skeptic to read the event code; either the Skeptic did not run or its messages were not captured. Until the synthetic market has enough names and event flags, and G0 reports an event or position count it requires to be non-zero, a G0 pass on these cards says little about look-ahead.

title: The release-session reaction drift reproduces on the same events in three book designs, and the long side alone shows it
statement: Three cards built on the same real-release-date reaction events (a long/short book, a fixed-slot long/short book, and a long-only tilt on positive reactions) each cleared the placebo bar with gross above cost and a positive sign in every third of the sample. They share events, so this is one piece of evidence seen three times, not three confirmations. What is new: the positive side alone carries drift, so the effect is not only a short-side artifact, and within the positive-only set it weakens from the earliest to the latest third while staying positive. The effect is real in an equal-weight event study but small next to cost: the market-neutral books lost to T-bills, and the long-only tilt on an always-invested core came nearest to a pass, beating the market on the point estimate with a reliable bound but not by the required margin.

title: G0 now reports real event counts and look-ahead cuts for event cards; Skeptic messages still absent
statement: K-0045 said G0 reported no event or position count and was vacuous for event cards on the 80-name synthetic market. For H-0031, H-0032 and H-0033 the G0 metrics contain events_in_dev (14678, 15554, 7524) that match the G1 event counts (14678, 15547, 7524) and an events_lookahead_failures block with 25 cuts and no failures, so the gate-side check appears to run on the real event set now. Not verified: where the 25 cuts fall (whether they hit event rows). The Builder-side lab try still shows zero events on the synthetic market (their summaries), and G0 for H-0010 to H-0030 stays as K-0045 described. cases.json again has no Skeptic message for any of the three cards although each Builder summary asked the Skeptic to read the event code; either the Skeptic did not run or its messages are not captured.

title: Fixed event slots did not close the gap between a passing event study and a failing market-neutral book
statement: Four cards cleared the event-study gate and then failed the strategy gate (H-0016, H-0019, H-0028, H-0031). H-0031 removed the first suspect of K-0042, weight normalization, with fixed risk-scaled slots and a liquid net hedge; exposure was about two fifths and the net Sharpe was still below T-bills, so the card's own stop rule fired. Remaining suspects: hedge basket not matched to the study's equal-weight benchmark, costs on names that just moved several deviations, squeezes, and cash handling (unverified whether idle cash earns the T-bill rate). The gate gives no gross/net or long/short split. The long-only tilt H-0033 came close, pointing at the short, hedge or cash side. Event gross covered cost by a modest multiple in both books. Do not file more market-neutral reaction-following books until the output decomposes.

title: Crypto forced-flow rebounds exist before stress but a taker cannot keep them
statement: The conditional rebound after fast, high-volume, taker-dominated moves in liquid crypto perps (H-0035, both directions) left a positive average trade after modeled taker costs and beat random-timed trades, so a liquidity-provision effect appears to exist. It did not survive costs at twice the model, and its profit sat in the first two thirds of the 2020-2022 dev period while the last third lost. Together with the hourly reversal finding of study mrel-1h (harvestable only as a maker) and the daily dip-buy H-0006 (could not tell), the pattern is that crypto reversal is paid to whoever provides liquidity at the stress moment and is small or negative for a taker who enters a candle later with optimistic slippage. The effect looked faster than the hold: the result halved with a one-candle later fill. Whether it is absent in sustained crashes is untested.

title: G2 random-timing null is deeply negative in two cards, so passing it may only measure costs
statement: In H-0007 (weekly US stocks) and H-0035 (fifteen-minute crypto perps) the random-entry or random-timing null passed with a median Sharpe far below zero. For H-0035 the strategy's modeled cost drag was about half of its gross, which implies a matched-turnover random book should lose roughly the size of the strategy's own Sharpe, not several times it; the null's median was several times worse. Either the null trades more or costs more than the real book, or the null is dominated by something other than timing. Until the null's turnover, exposure and cost per trade are reported next to the strategy's, a pass on this check should not be read as evidence of timing skill. Asked to the owner in the H-0035 message.

title: The point-in-time universe rule also forces early exits in crypto perp cards
statement: K-0032 recorded that the engine refuses weights outside the declared point-in-time universe for stock events. H-0035 shows the same rule on crypto_top_n: a position held across a universe update was refused at G0, and the Builder had to close such trades at the first decision row outside the universe, contradicting the card's 'closed on schedule' clause. The deviation touched few trades, but the clause cannot be honored and a Scout should not promise it. Event cards on a rolling top-n universe should state an exit rule that tolerates leaving the universe. Separately, the intraday data has no forward source, so such cards can pass at most G4.

title: Short-horizon effects that clear the pooled placebo test are usually weakest or reversed in the latest third of dev
statement: Across the lab's event studies that cleared or came near the placebo bar, the effect is typically largest in the earliest third of the dev period and smallest in the latest, in several cases with the opposite sign: month-turn beta, index inclusion, trading-window flow, short-horizon reversal, weekday mood in speculative stocks, twin-ETF gaps and perp funding crowding. Only earnings-reaction drift stayed positive in every third, and it also weakened. A pooled event study therefore overstates what a card can expect going forward, and the pooled pass hides one-episode results. A Scout should expect decay by default and state the latest-third sign as a kill condition. Three equal blocks of one history cannot separate publication decay from a change of regime or cost level.

title: The cost check now binds more often than the placebo test, and near-cost results are sensitive to the cost tier
statement: H-0030, H-0036 and H-0039 passed the placebo percentile (H-0039 by a hair) and failed only on gross against round-trip cost; H-0036 and H-0039 ended within a fifth of the cost, H-0030 well under. H-0037 failed both. The cost ratio prices the event legs only: hedge baskets, the weekend or overnight holds, and tier choices (taker spread, perp tier) enter only when a strategy runs, so a ratio close to one is neither a safe bound nor a refutation. Before filing a daily or weekly rotation of a taker book, a Scout should write down the expected gross per event against the cost tier of the instrument, and treat a card whose gross is a fraction of cost as untradable regardless of the placebo result. This extends K-0034 (placebo bar against cost) to the cost check itself.

title: H-0038 had events at G0 and none at G1; H-0039 got no universe at G0
statement: K-0047 said G0 events_in_dev matches the G1 event count. That still holds for H-0036 and H-0039 (counts agree to within a fraction of a percent) and for H-0037 (1040 against 1006). It fails for H-0038: G0 counted 241 events and passed its look-ahead cuts, G1 counted zero events with a null abnormal return, so the mechanism was never measured. Possible causes, unconfirmed: a two-instrument universe (TLT, SHY) leaves no peer set for the abnormal return; a tradable or universe mask is missing for the generic auction dataset (the catalog gives it no cost model and calls it signal only); an event definition used by G0 but not G1. Separately, H-0039 first crashed at G0 because the gate passed no crypto_top_n universe on the daily perp data; the Builder computed its own top twenty by 30-day dollar volume, so the event set may differ from the judge's universe definition. Skeptic messages are again absent for all four cards. K-0047 stands for its other points.

title: The G1 event study needs unmarked peers on each date: marking every universe instrument gives zero events
statement: H-0041 marked all five universe instruments on event dates, as its card said. The Builder tried it in the lab: marking five gave zero events, marking three gave zero, marking two gave events, and dates with only two unmarked instruments with data were dropped. The abnormal return is measured against the unmarked peers, so the judge seems to need at least three per date (inferred from behaviour, code not read). Same symptom as H-0038 (two-instrument universe, events at G0, none at G1, K-0054), which this makes the leading explanation. Consequences: the card as written could not run; the Builder narrowed the measured claim (SPY against IEF, not against TLT) and G1 and G0 event counts then agreed (482 both); nothing in the card schema warns of the peer rule. Also events() returns a single mask, so a declared complementary event set (equity drops on days when Treasuries fell) cannot be reported, the old diagnostic-channel gap again. Skeptic messages are absent for this card too.

title: Stress rebounds: positive on average, near generic drift, weakest lately
statement: A rebound after forced selling appears as a positive pooled average in three settings: daily crypto dip-buying (H-0006, could not tell), fifteen-minute crypto cascades (H-0035) and stocks against Treasuries after sessions where stocks fell and long Treasuries rose (H-0041). In each the effect is near, not clearly beyond, what time-shifted placebo windows give, and the latest third of dev is the weakest or negative, possibly because stress episodes ran on instead of reversing (not verified by an era or episode split). For the ETF case random windows already favour equities over Treasuries, so the raw gap overstates the event. Studies 6 and 7 found the same for VIX-conditioned reversal: a market-level bounce, not a selection effect, and no gain over holding the market. New stress-rebound cards in other assets are largely the same evidence again, not independent confirmations. A Scout should state how the design separates a one-off shock from a persistent crash.

title: lab try knows instruments named by the strategy (intraday crypto_top_n)
statement: Intraday crypto_top_n cards may name a leader or exclusion (e.g. BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT) in strategy.py. Since commit 405b0961 the Builder's lab try adds instrument-like string literals (…USDT) to the synthetic market; before, data.col('BTCUSDT') crashed in lab try (synthetic names were AAAUSDT..FFFUSDT) although real G0 on real data was unaffected. A Builder rewrite after such a block may not reuse earlier code (old workspace files are gone), so re-verify parity with the card's reference.

title: BTC-led altcoin catch-up is parameter-fragile in the lab
statement: The rule 'long lagging altcoins after a BTC hourly jump beyond k sigma, hold four hours' looks strong on the dev period at the primary setting but its edge needs a high threshold: lower thresholds lose most of it and the result is dominated by one sub-period. It failed G2 on neighbor stability and block concentration, while survival under delay and doubled costs was fine. A narrowed grid after the fact would be a new trial, not a rescue.

title: Cards imported from the owner's earlier research carry a contaminated holdout and an undercounted trial family
statement: H-0040 is the first card that is an earlier owner rule re-run through the lab (research 16 and 17, selected on data that includes the lab's holdout). The card says so and states that its family trial count misses at least dozens of earlier configurations. Consequences: the judge's trial counter and multiple-testing penalty see one trial where there were many; a G4 holdout pass would not be out-of-sample; only forward data after the owner's registration date is clean. The card also changed the leader, universe ranking, costs and fill timing, so it is a re-implementation, not a replication; the lab's result and the owner's can differ for that reason as well. Suggested handling: the Chair adds the earlier configurations to the family count, and a Scout or owner states the provenance on the card before the run, as here.

title: Short-horizon effects that clear the pooled placebo test are usually weakest or reversed in the latest third of dev
statement: Across the lab's event studies that cleared or came near the placebo bar, the effect is typically largest in the earliest third of the dev period and smallest in the latest, in several cases with the opposite sign: month-turn beta, index inclusion, trading-window flow, short-horizon reversal, weekday mood in speculative stocks, twin-ETF gaps and perp funding crowding. Only earnings-reaction drift stayed positive in every third, and it also weakened. New: the pattern also holds for a full strategy that passed its absolute and bootstrap bars, the BTC-led altcoin catch-up (H-0040), where the middle third carried most of the return and the latest third lost, so G2 killed it on concentration. The three crypto perp cards (H-0035, H-0039, H-0040) share one short dev window, a single boom-and-bust cycle, so their thirds are regimes rather than independent samples, and the latest third was the weakest in each. A pooled result therefore overstates what a card can expect going forward. A Scout should expect decay by default and state the latest-third sign as a kill condition. Three equal blocks of one history cannot separate publication decay from a change of regime or cost level.

title: G2 random-timing null is far below zero in three cards, so passing it may only measure costs
statement: In H-0007 (weekly US stocks), H-0035 and H-0040 (fifteen-minute crypto perps) the random-entry or random-timing check passed with a median Sharpe far below zero. In H-0035 the null was several times worse than the strategy's own cost drag would imply. In H-0040 it is less extreme: the strategy's modeled cost was a bit under two fifths of gross, which puts its cost drag in Sharpe terms at well under one, and the null's median was roughly one and three quarters times that. Either the null trades more or costs more than the real book (the strategy skips signals while a position is held and is invested a few percent of the time), or something other than timing dominates. The null's turnover, exposure and cost per trade are still not reported next to the strategy's, so a pass on this check should not be read as evidence of timing skill, and the percentile reached by an all-negative null is uninformative. The question to the owner from H-0035 is still open.

title: Zero events can pass G0 and then read as a mechanism failure
statement: Three cards ended on the event count with no mechanism result: H-0021 (empty by universe), H-0038 (events at G0, none at G1) and H-0043 (zero at G0 and at G1). H-0043 is new: G0 passed with zero events, and the signal was a two-sigma residual gap that fires regularly in any healthy series, so the cause is almost surely the inputs (ICE BofA spread coverage in the lab's FRED copy, the valid-day rule, or NaN propagation), not the market. The registry shows g1_mechanism_events, which a Scout can read as a failed mechanism. Suggested handling: G0 should flag a card whose events_in_dev is zero; the Builder should report events by year before submitting; the Archivist should confirm first-valid dates of long-history series. The card's fail-loudly coverage check cannot be point-in-time at G0.

title: Fed-calendar equity premia against bonds: positive on average, near the placebo bar, not tradable, weakest lately
statement: Two designs on the Fed's pre-announced calendar, the scheduled announcement sessions (H-0042) and the even-week cycle of FOMC time (H-0045), both gave a positive equity-over-bond or high-beta-over-low-beta average that was inside or just under the time-shifted placebo cloud. The two live at different horizons: the announcement design shows its gain on the announcement session only, while the cycle design shows nothing at one session and builds over several, so the cycle result is not the announcement-day effect again. Both are weakest in the latest third of dev, which includes publication, and gross is thin relative to cost. A design that marks both sides (even long, odd short) gives a placebo mean near zero, which is a cleaner test than the one-sided H-0042, where part of the gain was generic equity drift. A further Fed-calendar card on equities and Treasuries has a low prior unless it changes the instrument (index futures, equity-only comparison) or the horizon; this extends K-0060 without superseding it.

title: A strong mechanism pass did not carry over to a long-only always-invested tilt
statement: Several cards cleared the event-study gate and then failed the strategy gate (H-0016, H-0019, H-0028, H-0031, H-0046). K-0048 suspected hedge basket, shorts, costs and cash, because the long-only tilt H-0033 came close. H-0046 removes most of that: a long-only tilt on an always-invested book, no shorts, hedge or cash, with the strongest placebo score so far and gross several times cost, still lost to the constant mix on Sharpe. Remaining suspects: the study pools four equity ETFs against four bond peers while the book trades SPY and IEF only; the effect built over several sessions while the book held one; the earliest third carries most of the mean; and the benchmark or book construction is unverified (return, drawdown and Sharpe disagreed oddly; owner asked). A rough estimate suggests the Sharpe margin was within reach had the study effect carried over. Scouts should state the expected annual gain for the traded instruments only next to the required margin.

title: Macro-calendar cards on asset-class ETFs fail in three designs; reaction drift is single-stock only
statement: Three designs built on the scheduled US macro calendar (announcement-session beta premium, H-0042; even-week FOMC-cycle tilt, H-0045; cross-asset reaction drift, H-0047) all ended at the event-study gate. The first two gave a positive but unreliable average, weakest lately (K-0063). The third, which follows the release-day reaction instead of fixing a side, found the opposite sign: the most extreme reactions did slightly worse than peers over the next sessions, with the same sign in every third of dev and the placebo mean near zero. So continuation after scheduled news, the lab's best mechanism result in single stocks with real release dates (K-0046), does not appear across asset-class ETFs, consistent with the owner's daily lead-lag scan (mrel). The wrong-signed result is not an invitation to the mirror trade: its size is of the order of round-trip cost, and the test cannot tell whether release days matter or any large ETF day behaves this way (K-0056). Treat macro calendar x ETFs as a low prior unless the instrument or horizon changes.

title: Perp funding does not tell forced crash selling from informational selling on a daily horizon
statement: Two daily designs have used the perpetual-futures funding market as a state variable in liquid Binance perps over the 2020-2022 dev window. A cross-section on the funding level (H-0039) gave a small multi-day price effect that barely cleared the placebo bar and sat in one episode. A crash-day split on the change in funding (H-0049: flushed versus unflushed coins among same-day relative losers, both sides marked, same-date unmarked peers as the base, so the generic market bounce is netted out and the placebo mean sits near zero) gave nothing at the first day and the wrong sign at the multi-day horizons, worst in the latest third, the bear market. So once the generic stress bounce of K-0056 is removed, a funding-based flush label did not add a rebound and may have marked persistent selling. Funding looks like a weak and regime-dependent separator, not a reliable detector of forced liquidations. Whether it works at intraday frequency or for makers is untested, and the dev window holds one boom-and-bust cycle.

title: The G1 reason code can name the event count while the mechanism was measured and failed; the count was visible at G0
statement: H-0049 is registered as g1_mechanism_events (193 events against a minimum of 200), but G1 also measured the mechanism: abnormal return wrong-signed, placebo percentile 0.21, cost ratio negative, latest third clearly negative. A Scout reading only the registry would take it for a power or sparsity problem that more events could cure. This is the opposite of K-0062, where an empty event set reads as a mechanism failure. The G0 result already reported events_in_dev = 193, below the minimum, and the card had expected several hundred events a year while the judge found about 44 a year; no check compared the two before G1. Suggested handling: report all failing checks in the registry reason, flag at G0 or in the Builder summary when events_in_dev is under the G1 minimum, and have Scouts state an expected event count for the dev window and check it before filing (K-0032). Skeptic messages were again absent for this card (K-0054, K-0055).

title: Mechanical stock-bond flow: the study effect appeared only when the trigger was a large stock-bond move
statement: Three daily-ETF cards tried to trade mechanical stock-bond reallocation pressure. The month-end rule on month-to-date drift (H-0002) carried almost no edge. The threshold-drift trigger (H-0046) passed the event study clearly, but its events were large relative stock-bond move days, so generic spread reversal could not be separated from rebalancer flow, and the book lost to the plain mix. The volatility-control trigger (H-0050) removed that confound: the event day is quiet and the cause lies many sessions earlier. There the average was slightly wrong-signed, inside the placebo cloud, and negative in the latest third. The simplest reading is that the H-0046 pass was mostly generic reversal after large moves (K-0056), not rebalancer flow. The H-0050 sample was thin and clustered in high-volatility regimes, so this is a lean, not a refutation. A further mechanical-flow card on daily ETFs has a low prior unless the flow is observed where it trades (futures, closing auction) or a control separates it from stress reversal.

title: G1 event-count code can hide a measured mechanism failure; date tripwires cannot fire at G0
statement: H-0049 (193 events against a minimum of 200) and H-0050 (172 marked events on 43 event dates) are both registered as g1_mechanism_events, yet G1 measured the mechanism in both: wrong-signed average, placebo percentile far under the bar, negative cost ratio, weak latest third. A Scout reading the registry takes them for sparsity problems more events would cure; the sign says otherwise (the opposite of K-0062). New in H-0050: the card wrote its tripwire in event dates (flag if under 50 dates), but G0 reports marked events (four ETFs per date), so it showed 172 and the tripwire could not fire; the dates appeared only in G1 metrics. Both Scouts forecast event rates far above the real count. Skeptic messages were absent again. Suggested: list all failing checks in the registry reason; report event dates next to marked events at G0 and flag counts under the G1 minimum; Scouts state expected dates and marked events separately.

title: Macro-calendar cards fail in four designs; moving to a volatility ETP did not help
statement: Four designs on the scheduled US macro calendar have ended at the event-study gate: announcement-session beta premium (H-0042), even-week FOMC-cycle tilt (H-0045), cross-asset reaction drift (H-0047) and short volatility over release windows through a VIX-futures ETP (H-0052). The last was the route K-0063 and K-0065 left open. It gave a positive average, but placebo windows of the same instrument already earned over half of it through roll-down, the effect grew with the horizon like generic carry, and the first third of dev was flat while the middle third carried most (not the early-heavy decay of K-0060). The placebo bar lay above cost although gross was several times cost, because a volatility ETP is noisy. A release-time volatility crush is not visible in daily ETP bars. A further macro-calendar card on daily ETFs has a low prior; implied volatility or index futures measured directly are untested and not loadable.

title: Slow-horizon event studies: the placebo bar sits several times above cost, so only a large effect can pass G1
statement: H-0054 (about three-month residual momentum) and H-0055 (about two-month variance-risk tilt) are, as far as the lessons show, the first cards with a primary horizon beyond a month that reached a mechanism verdict. Both had gross several times round-trip cost, the right sign in every third and a placebo mean near or below zero, and both ended under the percentile bar (mid-eighties percentile) with a bar roughly seven times cost. At the five-session horizon of earlier cards the bar sat near cost (K-0034). The cloud widens with the horizon while cost does not, and monthly or weekly signals give overlapping windows with few independent episodes. The brief's one-to-six-month horizon therefore meets the least powerful form of the G1 mechanism test: an effect must be several times cost to pass, and near misses are 'cannot tell' (K-0026). A Scout should state the expected placebo bar next to expected gross and cost; widening the event set helps only if it adds independent dates. Whether G1 should use a horizon-aware bar for slow claims is a judge-design question for the owner.

title: Cross-market information-diffusion claims in liquid assets come out flat or wrong-signed from daily to monthly horizons
statement: Claims that news in one liquid market is priced late in another have not shown a delayed positive response at daily to monthly horizons. Statistical peer catch-up in US stocks (H-0013) was slightly negative, macro-release continuation across asset-class ETFs (H-0047) was wrong-signed in every third, and the oil-specific shock underreaction against Treasuries (H-0056) was wrong-signed in every third and grew with the horizon, ending in the lower tail of the placebo cloud. The owner's daily lead-lag scan (mrel) agrees. The one survivor to G2 is intraday crypto (H-0040), which then failed on stability. These are not power failures: both sides were marked and the placebo means sat near zero. They differ from the slow right-signed near misses (H-0054, H-0055), where the issue is a wide placebo bar (K-0071). Do not treat a wrong-signed result as an invitation to trade the mirror: the sign is dev-selected, the episodes are few and clustered, and the ETF peers carry stock-bond drift. A new card in this area should say why information would travel slowly through this particular channel, and what separates it from risk-on or reflation co-movement.

title: Multi-year reversal: absent in country equity ETFs, present for currency value in a short sample
statement: Two cards tested the same long-horizon reversal idea in different assets. Country equity ETFs sorted on multi-year past returns (H-0060) showed no reversal over the next quarter, and the sign was wrong in the early and middle thirds. Six G10 currency trusts sorted on distance from a five-year average spot (H-0062) showed cheap currencies beating rich ones, building with the horizon, positive in the populated thirds and clearly above the placebo cloud. The currency result has caveats that keep it from being a finding: the effective sample is only about nine years after the warm-up, value and carry are mixed (rich currencies in the period were low-yield), the score is nominal and the book could not reach the absolute Sharpe floor. If the split is real it fits an anchor-based story (purchasing power) working where a return-chasing story does not. The equity sort is also confounded with currency, since USD country ETFs carry both. A third long-horizon reversal card should say which anchor it uses and how it separates carry.

title: The G1 abnormal return is raw against unmarked peers, so a bucket with a different beta tests partly market direction
statement: The G1 event study compares marked instruments with unmarked peers in raw returns. A card whose distinctive claim is beta neutrality (H-0054, sizing enters only in the strategy), or whose marked set differs in beta from its peers (young coins in H-0058, R&D-intensive growth stocks in H-0059), is therefore tested on a bucket that also carries market-direction exposure. In H-0058 the sign followed the market cycle across the thirds (young coins led in the boom, lagged in the bear), as a beta difference would produce; in H-0059 the same-stock placebo removes the level of the style but not a time-varying beta. Inferred from the metrics, not tested with a beta-matched control. A Scout should state the expected beta gap between marked and peers and choose peers or events that neutralize it. Whether G1 should offer a beta-adjusted abnormal return is a judge-design question for the owner.

title: Signal history before the dev start or the ETFs' first date seems not to warm up the first signals
statement: H-0061 requested Moody's yields from 1986 for decisions from 2003 but reached G1 with 484 marked events against a forecast of 550 to 650, and its first dev third held far fewer events than the others, about its three-year minimum-observation rule. H-0062 requested FRED fixings from 1999 for ETFs listed in 2007; its strategy started in September 2011 (ETF start plus the 90 percent coverage rule on a five-year window), with 220 events against about 330 forecast and 4 in its first third. Both fit one cause: signal-only series reach the strategy only from the card's start, so warm-up eats the first dev years. Inferred from counts and dates; loader not read. Effects: shorter samples, an almost empty first block, a publication split with little earlier data. Until the owner confirms, Scouts should compute the first signal date from the card's own period.

title: Slow-horizon event studies: one clear pass, most failures wrong-signed or equal to the placebo mean
statement: Since K-0071, five more cards with a primary horizon of a quarter reached a mechanism verdict: H-0057 (about zero, decaying), H-0058 (wrong-signed), H-0059 (positive but equal to the same-stock placebo mean), H-0060 (wrong-signed) and H-0061 (wrong-signed, one crisis). H-0062 (currency value) passed with a placebo percentile near the top: gross about eight times cost against a bar about seven times cost, growing with the horizon. With the near misses H-0054 and H-0055 that makes eight slow verdicts: one pass, two near misses, five that more power would not cure. K-0071 stands for modest effects, but an effect of that size can pass, and most slow failures were signs or placebo-equal averages. Read a slow failure by its sign and placebo mean first, the bar second. The 60-session cap still shows only the first quarter of year-long claims.

title: Fifteen-minute crypto perp taker moves: a small edge in both directions, consumed within about a candle
statement: Two cards on taker-dominated, high-volume fast moves in liquid Binance perps took opposite sides and found a small positive average trade after modeled costs on dev: a rebound after extended moves (H-0035) and a continuation after breaks out of a compressed range (H-0063). Neither survived a one-candle later fill or doubled costs, and in both the latest third of dev was the weakest. Both selected the moment the aggressive flow is already visible in the candle, so what is left after the signal candle closes is small. Together with K-0049 and the hourly study mrel-1h, the pattern is that the payoff on this time scale goes to fast fills and makers, and a taker entering at the next open pays for the front of the move. The BTC-led catch-up over hours (H-0040) survived delay and doubled costs and failed on stability instead, so slower follower effects are not ruled out. Cards on this time scale should state the expected gross per trade after a one-candle delay, not only at the next open.

title: G2 random-timing null is far below zero in four cards; in H-0063 it matches cost drag
statement: In H-0007 (weekly US stocks), H-0035, H-0040 and now H-0063 (fifteen-minute crypto perps) the random-entry or random-timing check passed with a median Sharpe far below zero. In H-0035 the null was several times worse than the strategy's cost drag; in H-0040 about one and three quarters times. H-0063 allows a sharper reading: doubling costs lowered its Sharpe by about one and a half, which is its cost drag at the model, and the null median (about minus one and eight tenths, 95th percentile still below zero) sits close to that. So the null is roughly 'same trades, zero gross, normal costs', and a percentile of one means only that gross is positive, not that the timing pays for itself: the same book failed doubled costs, delay and neighbors. The null's turnover, exposure and cost per trade are still not reported next to the strategy's, so for H-0007 and H-0035 the gap to cost drag is unexplained. Read a pass as 'gross above zero', never as evidence of tradable timing; an all-negative null makes the percentile uninformative. The question to the owner from H-0035 stays open.

title: Return-sort effects in liquid US stocks stay below cost, except a pre-release reversal that faded
statement: Past-return sorts in liquid US stocks have been tried with reversal and continuation signs and many conditioners (news, turnover, intraday split, peers, earnings sessions removed, quarter-end window). Almost all gave effects far below round-trip cost or nothing (H-0007, H-0029, H-0030, H-0065). The exception is the reversal of the last few sessions just before a predicted earnings release (H-0064): the first conditioner whose event gross sat clearly above cost with a placebo mean near zero. It was strongest in the earliest third, wrong-signed in the latest, and the unhedged book earned far less than the event study implies. So K-0044 holds for slow and calendar conditioners, not for an event-window conditioner tied to inventory risk. A new conditioner should be argued from that risk, state the latest-third sign as a kill condition, and include a control sort at dates away from the event.

title: Information-diffusion claims in liquid assets come out flat or wrong-signed, also with a dated news event
statement: Claims that news in one liquid market is priced late in another have not shown a delayed positive response from daily to monthly horizons. Statistical peer catch-up in US stocks (H-0013) was slightly negative, macro-release continuation across ETFs (H-0047) and the oil shock against Treasuries (H-0056) were wrong-signed in every third. New: H-0066 replaced the undated peer move by a verified event (a large real earnings-release reaction) and looked only at peers that had not reported; the average was still inside the placebo cloud with a bar below cost, and longer horizons turned negative. So undated noise in the trigger was not the only reason for H-0013's failure. These are not power failures. Do not trade the mirror: the sign is dev-selected and episodes are few. A new card should say why information would travel slowly through this particular channel; explicit economic links are untested and not loadable.

title: On real earnings dates the events that cleared the placebo test sort on the stock's own price move
statement: Across the cards on real 8-K earnings dates, the mechanism tests that cleared the placebo bar condition on the stock's own price move at or just before the release: reaction drift (H-0028, H-0031, H-0033) and the pre-release reversal (H-0064). Cards that sort on a second variable or another stock did not: fundamentals, net flow, volume, delay or earnings change (H-0024, H-0026, H-0027, H-0032, H-0067) and correlated peers (H-0066). Date-only premia (H-0023) also failed. Hindsight pattern from a modest number of cards, not a tested rule. Every pass was small next to cost once built into a book, and most weakened by the latest third (K-0060). A Scout should expect a price-move trigger to be the only kind with a prior of passing the event study, and should expect the book to be the harder gate.

title: lab try cannot exercise cards that need the 8-K flag: its synthetic ea_reaction_day never equals one
statement: The Builders of H-0064, H-0066 and H-0067 each report that the synthetic ea_reaction_day in lab try is uniform noise between 0 and 10, never exactly 1, so lab try shows zero events and its checks are vacuous for these cards; they tested events, book and point-in-time behaviour on hand-made data (one temporarily rounded the flag). On real data G0 did report events (counts within a handful of G1's) and no look-ahead failures in 25 cuts, so G0 is the first meaningful check, and an event-logic bug would surface only there. Suggested: make the synthetic flag a sparse 0/1 event series so lab try produces events.

title: On real earnings dates only own-price-move events cleared the placebo test; no such book survived
statement: On real 8-K earnings dates the mechanism tests that cleared the placebo bar condition on the stock's own price move at or around the release: reaction drift (H-0028, H-0031, H-0033), the pre-release reversal (H-0064) and, new, the post-release give-back of year-long winners (H-0068). Sorts on a second variable or another stock did not (H-0024, H-0026, H-0027, H-0032, H-0067, H-0066), nor did date-only premia (H-0023). New: H-0068 shows a slow own-price sort can pass, but only at the margin, with the mean in the earliest third and the effect still building beyond the hold: slow drift, not an announcement effect. Its market-neutral book lost to T-bills like those of H-0028, H-0031 and H-0064; only the long-only H-0033 came near. Hindsight pattern, not a tested rule. State the expected annual gain of the book, not the per-event gap.

title: Stress rebounds: positive on average, near generic drift, weakest lately, also in currencies with both sides marked
statement: A rebound after forced selling shows as a positive pooled average in four settings: daily crypto dip-buying (H-0006), fifteen-minute crypto cascades (H-0035), stocks against Treasuries (H-0041) and, new, relative reversal among G10 currency trusts after equity down-shock days (H-0070). In each it is near, not clearly beyond, the time-shifted placebo, and the latest third of dev is weakest or negative. H-0070 marked both sides inside one asset class and standardized the trigger by trailing volatility, so generic drift was netted out; gross still covered little of cost and the placebo bar lay below cost, so it is not a power problem. Its horizon profile was flat early and larger only at ten sessions, the shape of slow drift, and the long leg was the higher-beta currency (K-0074), so a beta confound is the leading reading. New stress-rebound cards are largely the same evidence again.

title: Perp funding and the perp-versus-spot volume split both fail to separate forced from informational big moves
statement: Three daily designs in liquid Binance perps over the 2020-2022 dev window tried to tell forced selling or buying from informational moves. A cross-section on the funding level (H-0039) gave a small multi-day effect that barely cleared the placebo bar and sat in one episode. A crash-day split on the change in funding (H-0049) gave nothing at the first day and the wrong sign at multi-day horizons, worst in the bear-market third. A big-move split on the perp-versus-spot volume ratio, both directions and both classes marked so generic reversal and beta mostly cancel (H-0071), was slightly wrong-signed and inside the placebo cloud, more negative at longer horizons, and positive only in the boom third. The placebo bar lay under cost, so this is not a power problem. Neither observable, what leveraged traders pay or where the volume traded, marks forced flow; a perp-led surge may mark informed trading, and moves that look forced seem to persist rather than reverse. Open interest and liquidation data would observe forced flow directly but are not loadable, and intraday or maker-side versions are untested. The dev window holds one boom-and-bust cycle.

title: G1 needs at least three unmarked peers per date, so early event dates can be dropped at G1 but counted at G0
statement: H-0041 showed that marking every universe instrument gives zero events at G1 and that dates with only two unmarked instruments with data were dropped (inferred: at least three unmarked peers per date; code not read). H-0072 adds a partial form of the same rule: G0 counted 647 events in dev, G1 measured 514, a gap of about a fifth. Its peers list from 2002 (SHY), 2007-01 (SHV) and 2007-05 (BIL), so events before the third peer exists were most likely dropped at G1 while G0 and the strategy still use them. The mechanism verdict then covers only about 2007 onward, not the full period of the card, and K-0054's statement that G0 and G1 counts agree does not hold when peers start late. Scouts with late-listing peers should state the first date with three unmarked peers and the expected events from that date; a G1 reading should say which years the event study covered.

title: Family perp-leverage-crowding merged into short-term-reversal; H-0039 moves with it but tests a different mechanism
statement: On the Librarian's question the Chair staged a merge of perp-leverage-crowding into short-term-reversal, because H-0071 shares the forced-versus-informational-flow question with H-0049, H-0035 and H-0006. Families cannot be split, so H-0039 moves too, which only makes the multiple-testing penalty stricter. H-0039 itself is a different mechanism: a cross-sectional sort on the trailing funding level (crowded longs against crowded shorts, held for days), not a rebound or fade after a big move. It was decided at G1 on cost, so nothing else changes. A reader of the registry should not take H-0039 as another stress-rebound test; for the mechanism evidence see K-0085. Read lessons filed under the old family name as part of short-term-reversal for the trial count.

title: Short VIXY timing: the unconditional roll-down is the effect
statement: Two cards short the VIX-futures ETP VIXY on a timing rule: over scheduled macro-release steps (H-0052) and in steep contango of the implied-volatility curve measured directly from index options (H-0073). Both had positive averages with gross many times cost, and in both time-shifted placebos of the same instrument earned most of the average, so the rule added little beyond holding the short. Both effects grew roughly evenly with the horizon, the shape of carry, not of an event. K-0070 left implied volatility measured directly as an untested control; the slope is now that control for the carry reading and it does not rescue the idea. In H-0073 the effect was clearly weaker in the later thirds of dev (K-0060), so the roll-down itself may have shrunk. Untested: tail days and drawdown of a timed versus an untimed short, borrow cost, and the actual futures curve. A further short-VIXY timing card has a low prior unless it argues a tail-risk gain, not an average one.

title: Family macro-announcement-premium merged into variance-risk-premium-timing
statement: On the Librarian's question the Chair merged macro-announcement-premium into variance-risk-premium-timing, because the two short-VIXY cards (H-0052, H-0073) both found that same-instrument placebos earned most of the average (K-0088). The merge brings H-0042 and H-0045 into the shared count, so the family now holds six trials (3 + 3), which makes the multiple-testing penalty stricter and changes no past verdict. H-0055 stays where it was. Families cannot be split, so H-0042 and H-0045 are not short-VIXY tests: they are Fed-calendar equity-bond tilts (K-0063), and the mechanism evidence for them stays in K-0063 and K-0070. A reader should treat lessons filed under macro-announcement-premium as part of variance-risk-premium-timing for the trial count only. A new macro-calendar or VIXY card on this family starts with a heavier penalty than its name suggests.

title: CFTC speculator positioning through commodity and currency ETFs: levels and weekly changes both come out empty
statement: Two designs on the same CFTC non-commercial positioning and almost the same commodity, metal and currency ETFs found no tradable effect: monthly positioning levels against their own history (H-0057) and the weekly change in speculator net position traded for five sessions (H-0051). Averages were about zero or wrong-signed and inside the placebo cloud, with no consistent sign across the thirds of dev: the levels design was positive only in the earliest third, the changes design only in the latest. In H-0051 the short horizons were flat and only the longest leaned the predicted way. Likely reasons are the reporting lag (entry days after the as-of date), futures roll and tracking noise in the ETFs, and physical trusts that do not hold the futures. The published premiums concern futures, so this does not refute them. A third ETF-based CFTC card has a low prior unless it changes the instrument to the futures themselves or controls for the market's own past return.

title: A card whose data period starts before the dataset's first row is blocked and cannot be revised in BLOCKED_DATA
statement: H-0051 asked for the CFTC dataset from 2004-01-02, three days before its first report (2004-01-05). The card went to BLOCKED_DATA on the missing dataset, and the later period mismatch could not be fixed there because BLOCKED_DATA cards cannot be revised; the owner had to park it, reopen it and file a one-line version 2, about eight days after the card was created. Nothing else changed in the card. A Scout should read the first date of a new dataset in the catalog or from the Archivist before writing the period, and the framework could allow period-only revisions in BLOCKED_DATA or flag a period that starts before the dataset when the card is specified.

title: lab try cannot exercise weekly-report cards on the CFTC dataset: its synthetic COT series are daily random walks
statement: The Builder of H-0051 reports that the synthetic cftc_cot_legacy_1d series in lab try are daily random walks, so no pair of reports exactly seven days apart exists and the book has zero trades and zero events there; it tested legs, weights, the seven-day rule, fewer than six eligible ETFs, late listing and truncation on hand-built weekly reports. On real data G0 reported events (about 2100) and no look-ahead failures in 25 cuts, and G1 counted nearly the same events, so G0 was the first meaningful check. Same kind of gap as K-0082 (synthetic 8-K flag never equal to one). Suggested: make synthetic report series weekly, stamped with a Friday release, so lab try produces events. The Builder also used the loader's usable-session date as the release date; whether the loader stamps holiday and shutdown delays correctly was not measured by any gate.

title: S&P 500 membership-change reversal: two designs end just under the placebo bar, with slow build and a faded latest third
statement: Two designs on the forced trading around S&P 500 membership changes in liquid US stocks, additions only (H-0017) and additions plus deletions read inside LIQ-500 (H-0022), both showed the predicted sign, a gross effect well above cost and a placebo mean near zero, and both landed just under the placebo percentile bar, with a bar above cost. Both effects were small in the first sessions and larger at the longest horizons, so the reversal is slower than a five-session hold, and in both the latest third of dev was weakest (about zero in the second). Adding the deletion leg gave more events but did not remove the near miss. They share most of their events, so this is one piece of evidence seen twice. Mandated-flow events remain the nearest thing to a live effect in the large-cap short-horizon cross-section (K-0024), but the gate cannot confirm them with a few events per month. Further tests on the same membership events are retries; a card needs a slower horizon argued from the build-up, or many more events.

title: Reaction drift is specific to earnings releases: large moves on non-earnings 8-K sessions show none
statement: On real earnings-release sessions, following a large standardized own-price reaction drifts in the same direction (H-0028, H-0031, H-0033). The same rule applied to sessions with a filed non-earnings 8-K (H-0034) gave a slightly wrong-signed average, inside the placebo cloud, with signs mixed across thirds and horizons beyond the first sessions leaning negative. Moves on sessions with no earnings release at all reverse slightly (H-0030). So a filing-identified news event did not turn reversal into drift: what separates the earnings case may be the scheduled date, the consensus benchmark and the attention an earnings release draws, not the presence of news. Caveats: the 8-K item types are pooled and the filing session can come after the press release, so the dated reaction may be a tail or a routine filing. Not tested: single item types, press-release timestamps, a news-versus-no-news comparison within the same stocks. Dated news outside earnings now has one flat verdict; a further filing-based drift card needs a reason that the item type is a surprise.

title: PIT S&P 500 mask now reaches liq_n cards; G0 counted more events than G1
statement: K-0032 recorded that H-0022 could not run because the PIT S&P 500 mask was not delivered to LIQ-500 cards. The owner reopened it after extras['sp500_member'] was deployed (prod ba7c4c2), the Builder read it directly, G0 passed with no look-ahead failures in 25 cuts, and G1 measured the mechanism, so the both-direction index-change test is feasible and a deleted stock that stays liquid can be held. The other parts of K-0032 stand: events on young or departing stocks that never sit in the declared universe give an empty set (H-0021), and weights outside the declared universe are refused (H-0018, K-0051). New: G0 counted 453 events in dev and G1 measured 395, about an eighth fewer, with zero events lacking controls. Cause unconfirmed: the G1 window start, the forward window at the end of dev, or a peer rule like K-0086. Scouts should expect G1 to cover somewhat fewer events than G0 reports.
