title: ICE BofA spread series in the lab's FRED copy are empty in dev
statement: The G0 check of H-0075 reported fred_macro.BAMLC0A0CM and fred_macro.BAMLH0A0HYM2 as series without a single value in the dev period, with first valid value 2023-10-04 (FRED serves only a short ICE BofA history). This confirms the cause K-0062 suspected for H-0043, whose zero events came from the spread inputs, not from the market. The catalog entry for fred_macro lists both fields and a range from 1998 but does not say they start in 2023, so a Scout cannot see it. Separately, that G0 failure appeared on H-0075 although the card requested only DGS10; a re-run then passed. Cause not known (inferred: a whole-dataset check at that moment). Scouts should not use ICE BofA OAS series for any dev period before 2023, and the Archivist should add the start dates of these two series to the catalog known_biases. H-0043's question about credit ETF gaps stays untested.

title: G1 now gives a gross/net split; H-0044 shows a positive event study beside a negative gross book
statement: Earlier lessons (H-0028, H-0031) said the gate gave no gross versus net or long versus short split. H-0044's G1 result has one: gross Sharpe, net Sharpe, each leg's Sharpe and the yearly cost drag. It shows what K-0064 suspected: costs were a minor part of the loss. The book was negative before costs and in both legs, while the event study of nearly the same window was positive and just above the placebo bar. So the gap between study and book is construction (weights set by signal size versus equal weights by sign, exit at the next open versus the fix-day close, one shared dollar bet across six currencies) or a bug, not cost. Also: when a strategy is run, the G1 checks list holds only strategy checks, so a mechanism pass or near miss is visible only in the metrics block. Builders should report the event-study mean next to the book's gross mean per window on the same dates. A reconciliation question went to the owner.

title: The registry shows one failed G1 check; sparse event-slot books also need exposure arithmetic in the card
statement: H-0077 is registered as g1_mean_exposure (mean exposure about 0.11 against a floor of 0.2), but its G1 result also failed the absolute Sharpe floor (net about 0.39, gross about 0.58, floor 0.5), while the bootstrap bound and excess checks passed. A Scout reading only the registry code would take it for a sizing problem that bigger slots cure; since Sharpe is roughly scale-free, they would not. Same pattern as K-0069 (the code hides what was measured). Cause of the thin exposure: G1 counted 658 events on 278 dates against a forecast of 1300 to 2700, and the book capped at five slots of seven percent each, so the average book held a fraction of the forecast. Rule for cards: write expected events per year, hold, slot weight and slot cap, and compute mean exposure (events x hold / 252 x weight) next to the absolute Sharpe floor, and state that gross Sharpe must clear the floor with margin before costs and hedge drag. Suggested: list every failing check in the registry reason.

title: Wrapper gaps revert where no arbitrage link exists: closed-end funds cleared the placebo test, twin ETFs did not
statement: Two wrapper cards in family etf-premium-arbitrage differ in the arbitrage link. Twin ETFs holding the same basket, where authorized participants close gaps (H-0037), showed a small gap reversion inside the placebo cloud and below cost. National municipal closed-end funds, which have no creation or redemption link, faded after a shock relative to the open-end muni ETF anchor (H-0077): the average sat far above the placebo cloud, gross was well above cost, the sign was positive in every third of dev, and it built across horizons up to the longest. It weakened from the earliest to the latest third, as K-0060 expects. Caveats: the event study measures the marked fund raw against unmarked peers, so a beta difference is not netted (K-0074); the fund list leans to survivors; events cluster on few dates; the book lost on exposure and Sharpe, not on cost (K-0097), and the hedge leg lost money alone. Wrapper evidence is the Scout's ground for this family, but one pass is not a finding about tradability.

title: Closed-end fund gaps revert against their ETF anchor in two asset classes; both books still fail at G1
statement: Two cards in family etf-premium-arbitrage marked a closed-end fund after a large relative shortfall against an open-end ETF anchor: national municipal funds against the muni ETF (H-0077) and single-country equity funds against their country ETFs (H-0078). Both cleared the placebo test far above the cloud, with gross several times cost and a positive sign in every third of dev. Both weakened from the earliest to the latest third (K-0060) but the latest stayed positive. Both kept building beyond the one-week hold, up to roughly two weeks. In both the ETF hedge lost money alone and the book failed G1 on thin mean exposure and on the absolute Sharpe floor, which was missed even before costs. So the gap reversion looks like a replicated event-study regularity where no creation or redemption link exists (twin ETFs with such a link showed little, H-0037), but it is sparse and clustered, and a flat-otherwise slot book cannot turn it into an absolute Sharpe of the required size. Caveats: raw returns against unmarked peers (K-0074), fund lists lean to survivors, events cluster on shared dates, no one has checked ticker reuse. Supersedes the single-pass reading of K-0099.

title: Reported mean exposure of a paired fund-ETF book is about half the card's gross arithmetic; the cause is unknown
statement: H-0078 forecast about 0.5 mean gross exposure (60 events a year, 5-session hold, 0.25 long plus 0.25 short per event, cap 2 events). G1 counted 1263 events on 496 dates and 813 position entries over 5283 sessions, close to the event forecast, yet reported mean exposure 0.199, just under the 0.2 floor. Entries x hold / sessions x 0.5 gross would give about 0.39; entries x hold / sessions x 0.25 gives about 0.19. So either mean_exposure counts one leg (or half the gross) of a paired book, or position_entries counts legs, or the cap and held-fund rule removed more than the entry count shows. Not resolved from the metrics; code not read. K-0098 had asked cards to write exposure arithmetic, and this card did, and still missed by a factor of two to three, so the arithmetic is only reliable if the gate's definition is known. The same ambiguity may sit behind H-0077's thin exposure. Also: both fund-class cards failed the absolute Sharpe floor even gross, so the exposure code in the registry hides the binding failure (K-0069, K-0098). Owner: please state whether mean_exposure is gross, long-only or net for paired books, and what position_entries counts.

title: Sharadar SFP lacks some delisted closed-end funds (CH, MF); the card's data check passes at DATA_READY and fails at G0
statement: H-0078 listed 24 fund-ETF pairs on purpose to include delisted funds and reduce survivorship. G0 failed the first version with g0_no_data_adapter because CH and MF are not in Sharadar SFP; the owner removed both pairs and re-filed (version 2), about 14 hours of cycle time lost. The catalog check (DATA_READY) resolves datasets, not tickers, so a Scout cannot see ticker coverage before G0. What stays unchecked: ticker reuse after delisting (GCH, IF, TTF, SGF, ISL, TKF, BZF, SNF, and others were flagged by the card and the Builder), because the Builder has no data access and no gate reports first and last price dates per ticker. Missing funds are a data limit, not a selection, but they lean the fund list toward survivors, in the same direction as H-0077's list. Suggested: the Archivist reports first and last price date per instrument for named-ticker cards, and the DATA_READY check flags tickers absent from the dataset.

title: Closed-end fund gaps revert in a pooled seven-class book; only the net Sharpe floor fails
statement: A pooled book of closed-end funds from seven classes, long after a large shortfall against a beta-adjusted ETF anchor and short the anchor, again cleared the placebo test at the top of the cloud, with gross several times cost and a positive sign in every third. The middle third, which likely holds 2008, was strongest and the latest weakest but positive. Muni and country funds reuse the event type of H-0077 and H-0078, so this is partly the same evidence, not an independent confirmation. Pooling cured exposure and entry counts and passed the bootstrap check, but net Sharpe stayed under the absolute floor while gross cleared it: cost of thinly traded funds took the margin. The anchor short lost money alone again, so the long leg may include asset-class beta (K-0074). The effect was small at one session and built over about two weeks, so it is not a one-day bounce.

title: Mean exposure of paired slot books fits entries x hold / sessions x leg weight
statement: H-0079 adds a second data point to K-0101. The card forecast mean exposure 0.25-0.30 on a one-leg count and 0.5-0.6 on gross; G1 reported 0.339 with 1192 entries over 4783 sessions, hold 5, weight 0.25 per leg. The formula entries x 5 / 4783 x 0.25 gives 0.31. H-0078 reported 0.199 with 813 entries over 5283 sessions; the formula gives 0.19. Both readings left open in K-0101 (entries count slots and exposure one leg, or entries count legs and exposure gross) give this same formula, so it can be used for forecasting while the definition stays unconfirmed. Until the owner answers, cards should compute exposure this way. The question in K-0101 stays open.

title: Wrapper-gap reversion shows in closed-end funds but not in ETFs
statement: In the etf-premium-arbitrage family the gaps that reverted were closed-end fund gaps against an ETF anchor (H-0077, H-0078, H-0079, K-0103), where no creation or redemption link exists. ETF gaps did not: twin ETFs (H-0037) fell short of the placebo bar, and a credit, EM, muni or loan ETF far below what SPY and IEF implied (H-0080) did not rebound, with a wrong-signed average at every horizon even though the test leaned its way (K-0074). Daily closes against liquid factor proxies are probably not a mispricing signal. H-0043 stays untested; H-0080 is its nearest replacement. A fair test needs premium to NAV, not loadable.

title: lab try cannot exercise cards that pair perps with spot: the synthetic market has no spot columns and no '.P' ids
statement: The Builder of H-0082 reports that the synthetic market in lab try has no spot instruments and no '.P' perp ids, so the spot-seasoning rule finds no pairs and lab try shows zero events and zero exposure; the logic was tested on hand-made data. This is the third data family with the same gap after the 8-K flag (K-0082) and the weekly CFTC reports (K-0092). On real data G0 then crashed once on the missing spot history (K-0075) and, after the fix, reported events within a handful of the G1 count (366 against 363) and no look-ahead failures in 25 cuts. So the first meaningful check of such cards is G0 on real data, and a data problem costs a full cycle. Suggested: give the synthetic market spot twins for its perps with a '.P' naming, listed at staggered dates, so lab try can produce events.

title: Newly available crypto coins did not underperform liquid peers in the dev window, in three designs
statement: Three cards shorted newly available Binance coins in different forms: young spot listings against seasoned ones (H-0004, decided on the strategy, could not tell), perps aged between one month and one year (H-0058, wrong-signed) and the first weeks after a perp launch of a coin with a seasoned spot pair (H-0082, wrong-signed). In both event studies the marked coins did not lag the other liquid perps on average; the sign followed the market cycle or alternated across thirds, and the wrong-signed effect grew with the horizon, the shape of trend or beta and not of a listing pump or a relief of short-sale constraints. Both used raw returns against unmarked peers (K-0074), so beta and attention are the leading readings, but no beta-matched control was run. All of it sits in one boom-and-bust window (K-0006). A further short-the-new-coin card has a low prior unless it neutralizes beta and prior run-up or changes the window.

title: Signal-only history before the view start is not delivered (H-0082 G0 crash)
statement: H-0082 requested Binance spot bars from 2017 as a signal-only dataset to verify that each coin's spot pair was seasoned before its perp launch. Its first G0 run crashed with 'view starts too late for the spot seasoning rule'. The Builder reports that the view starts at the perp panel's first date, so the spot history before it is not delivered although the catalog holds it. This is the direct confirmation of the cause K-0075 inferred from event counts (H-0061, H-0062). Consequences: any rule on a first-bar date, listing age or long look-back taken from a signal-only dataset is left-censored at the view start. The Builder had to count seasoning only when provable, so perp launches in roughly the first half year of dev were excluded for a data reason (longer for a stricter age rule), and G2 neighbors with a longer age lose early events too. The G1 event count came out well under the card's forecast, which fits but does not prove this cause. Scouts should compute first valid dates from the view start, not from the dataset range; the owner should either deliver signal-only history before the dev start or state in the catalog that it is not delivered.

title: Monthly-formation, quarter-horizon stock sorts: the placebo bar is about the size of the literature's whole spread
statement: H-0083 had tens of thousands of marked events on only a few hundred monthly dates with overlapping quarter-long windows. Its placebo cloud was wide: the upper bar was about 0.46 % per event, the observed side-adjusted average about 0.23 %, and the card's own forecast of the effect was 0.25-0.5 %, so even a true effect at the forecast's top would sit at the bar. The card said in advance that the bar would bind, and it did. Event count does not narrow the cloud (K-0026, K-0034): what counts is the number of non-overlapping dates. Same design family as H-0054 (right sign, bar above cost) and H-0059 (equal to the placebo mean). A card on a monthly sort with a quarter horizon should write down the expected effect next to the bar of earlier cards of this design, and treat a forecast below the bar as a card that can only end in 'cannot tell'. A cheaper test is a design that raises the number of independent dates (shorter horizon with non-overlapping windows, or several asset classes) or a stricter match that lowers the cloud.

title: Net repurchasers versus issuers: filing-anchored pass, no release flow, no slow drift
statement: The same repurchaser-versus-issuer sort was tested at three anchors in LIQ-500. Anchored to the quarterly filing, a five-session spread cleared the placebo bar clearly (H-0019). Anchored to the real release it did not, built slowly and reversed lately (H-0027). As a slow style premium, the route K-0041 left open, new entries to the extreme quintiles over a quarter (H-0086) averaged below same-stock placebos, were slightly negative in the first weeks, and faded from clearly positive in the earliest third to clearly negative in the latest. Reading: the filing-anchored pass was filing-linked news or an early-era effect, not a trading-window flow and not a drift visible in large caps. Caveats: the placebo bar lay well above cost, repurchasers have lower beta than issuers so late bull years bias the raw comparison (K-0074), no split by side was reported, and the year-long hold was never simulated. Treat the family as closed for event-study cards in LIQ-500 unless beta-neutral, side-split or in less covered stocks.

title: Slow monthly stock sorts: four designs, none passed; entry-only events widen the placebo cloud
statement: H-0086 is the fourth slow monthly-formation sort of liquid US stocks to end at the mechanism test (after H-0054, H-0059, H-0083): near misses with a bar above cost (H-0054, H-0083), right-signed but equal to the same-stock placebo (H-0059), and now below the placebo mean (H-0086). K-0109 said a card whose forecast is at or below the bar can only end in 'cannot tell'; H-0086 cited it, forecast an effect near the bar, and observed far less. New: to avoid the persistent-state trap of H-0059 it marked only new entries to the extreme quintiles. That left a few thousand events on a few hundred dates, and the placebo bar came out clearly wider than in H-0083 (inferred cause: fewer events per date, more dispersed stocks; not tested). So the cure for placebo-equals-level costs power, and a Scout should forecast the bar for the entry design, not copy it from a state design. Independent dates and dispersion matter, not event counts (K-0026, K-0034).

title: Currency value predicts country returns over a quarter in two vehicles, but neither dollar-neutral book is a strategy
statement: Country equity ETFs sorted on their own past return showed no reversal (H-0060). A five-year-average value score in G10 currency trusts passed the mechanism test (H-0062). The same score, measured only in FX and applied to unhedged country equity ETFs, also passed it (H-0088): above the placebo cloud, gross several times cost, positive in every third, so the local equity leg did not offset the currency recovery over a quarter. This answers the question K-0073 left open. The two currency cards share the signal, so this is one piece of evidence seen twice, on a short sample with few value cycles and a nominal score mixed with carry. Neither book became a strategy: the trust book missed the absolute Sharpe floor, and the equity book earned about T-bill returns, gross near zero, the long leg's gain mirrored by the short leg's loss. Study and book disagree for reasons not separated: G1 sees only the first quarter of a year-long hold, leg betas were not reported, and the book is in cash until the first signal. A further currency-value card has a low prior unless it reconciles study and book, hedges equity beta, or separates value from carry.

title: Scout event-count forecasts too high in four cards; joint tails of correlated variables are worst
statement: H-0049, H-0050 (K-0069), H-0077 (K-0098) and H-0089 all forecast far more events than the judge counted. H-0089 (taker-flow absorption, Binance perps) forecast hundreds of trades, made 17 in 2020-2022 against a minimum of 300 and died at G1 (g1_trades). Its event was a joint tail of extreme taker imbalance, heavy volume and a flat or opposite return, variables its own mechanism says move together. Scalping cards have no mechanism_test and G0 gave no trade count, so the miss surfaced only at G1; lab try gave zero events too (as K-0082, K-0092, K-0106). Scouts should state events per year for each condition and the intersection, and expect a joint tail of correlated variables to be far rarer than the parts suggest. Suggested: report trades by year at G0, and make synthetic volume, taker share and return correlated.

title: Scout event-count forecasts too high in five cards; rare-instrument definitions worst
statement: H-0049, H-0050, H-0077, H-0089 and now H-0090 forecast far more events than the judge counted (K-0069, K-0098, K-0113). H-0090 (share-class pairs found by return correlation in LIQ-500) forecast 600 to 1200 pair events and 3 to 8 pairs at a time; G0 and G1 both counted 66 events on 30 dates (about 3 a year) against a minimum of 200, roughly an order of magnitude off. The card named 'too few pairs' as the likeliest death and wrote a tripwire (under 100 entries), yet nothing let anyone see the count before G1: G0 reports events_in_dev without comparing it to the G1 minimum, and lab try found no pairs in synthetic data (as K-0082, K-0092, K-0106). The Builder also applied the stricter of two contradictory missing-data clauses (all 126 sigma days valid, not 100), which only lowers the count. Scouts should state events per year for each condition and for their intersection, expect a rare-instrument definition (both classes in the universe, extreme correlation, large gap) to be far rarer than the parts suggest, and avoid contradictory clauses. Suggested: G0 flags events_in_dev below the G1 minimum and reports events (and pairs) by year.

title: Subscription 'session limit' errors now pause agent runs
statement: The Claude subscription window error ('You've hit your session limit, resets 7am UTC') was not in RATE_LIMIT_WORDS, so no pause followed and every 30-minute cycle burnt another agent slot (4 Scout runs on 2026-10-30, 2 Builder runs on 2026-10-27). Since commit dac6ed66 the phrase triggers the same rate_limit_pause_hours pause as a 429.

title: Long Bash commands are waited for, not backgrounded (Archivist lab fetch)
statement: Claude Code moves a Bash command that outlives its timeout (2 min default) to the background; the Archivist then polled it with Monitor, sleep and Read of /tmp, each a policy violation, and four runs a night were discarded from 2026-10-27 on, which left every BLOCKED_DATA card stuck. Since commit d980f31c agents run with BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS of 15 minutes. The cause is inferred from the violation pattern, not from a transcript; if Archivist runs still end in policy violations after 2026-10-31, it is wrong.

title: lab try adds instruments named in the strategy to the daily crypto_top_n market
statement: A daily crypto_top_n card that reads a named instrument (the BTC factor BTCUSDT.P, a leader) crashed lab try G0 because the synthetic market held only SYNxxUSDT names, although real G0 was unaffected. Since commit 51536516 the daily lab try adds the instrument-like literals of strategy.py and diagnostic.py, as the intraday one already did (K-0057); the .P suffix is accepted.

title: The gate again passed no crypto_top_n universe at G0 on daily perp data (H-0081, after H-0039)
statement: H-0081's first G0 run (run 179) crashed because data.universe was None on binance_perp_1d, with the strategy raising 'needs the crypto_top_n point-in-time universe'. H-0039 hit the same crash (K-0054), so it recurred about two weeks later. The card also requested the signal-only fred_macro series VIXCLS; whether that matters is not known. The Builder wrote a fallback that rebuilds the top thirty from 30-day median dollar volume, noting that it may differ from the judge's definition; the Builder's later rewrite after the lab try fix (K-0117) reads data.universe. The summaries do not say which version produced the passing G0 run (run 180), so the event set may or may not be the judge's universe; G0 and G1 counted the same 1802 events, which fits the same definition at both gates but does not prove it. The crash cost one cycle. Suggested: the gate always passes the card's declared crypto_top_n universe on daily perp data; G0 reports which universe the strategy used.

title: Daily reversal in liquid crypto perps: four conditioners found none
statement: Daily designs on the top perps (2020-2022 dev) conditioned the big moves on funding level (H-0039), funding change (H-0049), perp-versus-spot volume (H-0071) and, new, a US implied-volatility stress gate with both sides marked (H-0081). None gave an average clearly above the placebo cloud with the predicted sign; H-0039 barely cleared, in one episode. In H-0049, H-0071 and H-0081 longer horizons turned negative, the shape of continuation. The placebo bar lay under cost in H-0071 and H-0081, so not a power problem. A positive third was a different third each time: regimes of one boom-and-bust cycle (K-0060). The unconditional daily reversal among these perps was never reported and is the missing control. Open interest and liquidations are not loadable; maker-side reversal (K-0049) and smaller pairs are untested.

title: Scout forecasts of events, regime days and cost ran too high in six cards
statement: H-0049, H-0050, H-0077, H-0089 and H-0090 forecast far more events than counted (K-0069, K-0098, K-0113); H-0090 forecast 600-1200, counted 66 on 30 dates. H-0081 adds: the VIX gate was expected on 35-45 percent of dev days, 400-500 dates, 4000-6000 events; G0 and G1 counted 1802 events on 207 dates, about a fifth of days (inferred). The card put the liquid-perp round trip at 25-35 bps; G1 used about 91 bps (cost model not read). Gross per event was about 3 bps, so it died on either cost. Scouts should count regime days from the actual series inside the usable period, state events per year per condition and intersection, and take the round trip from the catalog cost tier of the weakest instrument. Suggested: G0 flags events below the G1 minimum and reports events by year.

title: Holders' capital-gain overhang does not predict a short-horizon edge in liquid US stocks: two designs, both wrong-signed
statement: Two designs gated the news response of liquid US stocks by holders' unrealized gain. H-0009 followed volume-shock moves that agreed with the 12-month gain and lost money. H-0091 used real earnings-release reactions and long gain-overhang, short loss-overhang stocks, a contrast built to cancel generic reaction drift; its average was wrong-signed, below every time-shifted placebo, negative in every third of dev and at every horizon, and absent in the first session. The shape is slow drift, not an announcement effect, and fits the winner give-back of H-0068 (K-0083) because overhang is mostly a past-winner marker. A beta gap between legs (K-0074) was not neutralized; no split by news sign or no-release control sort was run. So a disposition channel is not supported in large caps over days, and the opposite sign is not shown to be an effect either. A new overhang card should separate good-news and bad-news cells and match legs on beta and past return.

title: Scout wall-clock timeouts: 15 % of runs hit 900 s; a normal run takes ~430 s
statement: Between 2026-10-05 and 2026-11-01, 16 of 107 completed Scout runs ended in a wall-clock timeout at the default 900 s (Builder, Librarian: none), clustered by day (10-27: 5, 10-30/31: 2 each), and on 10-30/31 timeouts were followed by session-limit failures. The first Scout run after the fix took 431 s and 22 turns, so 900 s left only ~2x headroom. Scout now has timeout_s 1500 and is told to do at most 3 WebSearch calls; the cause of the clusters (slow API vs a stuck search) is not verified. lab invocations now shows wall time and turns.

title: Rate-limit pause ends at the reset time named in the error, not after a fixed 5 h
statement: A session-limit failure ('resets 7am (UTC)') now pauses agent runs until that reset time (orchestrator.pause_until), capped at rate_limit_pause_hours; a message without a reset time still pauses for the full 5 h. Before, a limit at 06:35 blocked runs until 11:35 although the quota returned at 07:00. Untested in production until the next session limit.

title: lab fetch takes seconds for single-endpoint sources, minutes for paginated ones
statement: Existing fetchers run in 0.4-7 s (FRED, Treasury, DefiLlama, CFTC: 1-4 requests). Upbit answers in ~1.4 s per request, so a paginated multi-coin source (~300 requests, estimated, not run) needs ~7 min; the framework caps a fetch at 900 s and 500 requests. Archivist timeout_s was raised 1500 -> 3000 on 2026-11-01 because 3 Archivist runs timed out at 1500 s after the Bash backgrounding fix (K-0116); whether 3000 s is enough is not yet known.

title: Mean exposure of a filing-season event book came out well below entries x hold x weight / sessions
statement: K-0104 found that mean exposure of slot books fits entries x hold / sessions x slot weight (H-0078, H-0079). H-0092 does not fit: 16204 entries, hold 5, slot weight 0.04, 5437 decision dates (5787 observations) give an arithmetic gross of 0.56-0.60, while G1 reported a mean exposure of 0.36, and the card forecast 0.4-0.55. Two readings, not separated: the card's gross cap of 1.0 scaled down all entries of peak filing-season sessions (events cluster in a few weeks per quarter), or the reported exposure nets long against short positions. Either way, a clustered event book is invested less than the arithmetic says, and the scaled slots are smaller than the card's weight. Cards with clustered events should forecast exposure from the busiest weeks, not from the annual average, and state which exposure definition they use. The same card forecast events (about 14000-16000, counted 16330) and the round trip (12-15 bps forecast against about 12 bps modelled) correctly, which fits the advice of K-0098 and K-0120. The exposure definition question of K-0101 stays open.

title: Filing-anchored fundamentals sorts clear the placebo test in LIQ-500 twice, and both books stay near cash
statement: Two sorts with different content, net repurchasers against issuers (H-0019) and low against high quarterly accruals (H-0092), were both timed to the quarterly filing and held for a week in LIQ-500. Both cleared the same-stock placebo bar with gross above round-trip cost, and both books ended near T-bills (K-0064). They share filing dates, universe and seasons, so this is one piece of evidence seen twice. H-0019 faded era by era, while H-0092 was positive in every third, so the early-era reading in K-0110 is weaker. H-0092 effect was present in the first session and kept building, a slow reaction to filed information, neither flat nor front-loaded. The release-anchored sort (H-0027) and the slow style (H-0086) failed, so the anchor matters. In H-0092 the unbalanced short leg lost (K-0074). A further market-neutral filing sort in LIQ-500 has a low prior; a long-only tilt, beta-matched legs or less covered stocks are untested.

title: A predicted-release fundamentals sort cleared the placebo bar but not cost, and grew rather than decayed
statement: K-0083 found that on real 8-K dates only sorts on the stock's own price move cleared the placebo test. Earnings seasonality (H-0093) sorts on a second variable and cleared the percentile narrowly, with a placebo mean near zero and a bar below cost; the composite sort H-0032 did not. Its shape fit the claim (small early, larger by the end of the week, flat beyond) but gross stayed below round-trip cost. The latest block was the strongest, the reverse of K-0060, yet the first block had almost no events, so only two blocks are usable. This weakens K-0083 without refuting it. The date hit rate was never measured. A further predicted-window fundamentals sort in LIQ-500 has a low prior unless gross is argued clearly above cost.

title: Supply-side crypto sorts did not find the expected laggard in four designs; persistent coin identity carries the average
statement: Four cards tried to short coins on a supply-side characteristic: young spot listings (H-0004, could not tell), perps aged between one month and one year (H-0058, wrong-signed), the first weeks after a perp launch (H-0082, wrong-signed) and, new, the fastest token supply growth within beta halves (H-0085). In H-0085 the time-shifted placebo of the same coins was about as negative as the marked average, so the sort picks persistent coin identity (old slow-issuance coins against emission-heavy ones) and says nothing about timing. In the dev window the slow-issuance side lagged, and the sign swung with the cycle across thirds, as in H-0058, so beta-matching legs by halves did not cure the confound that K-0074 names. Only protocol issuance was visible, not vesting unlocks. All of it sits in one boom-and-bust window (K-0006). A further overhang or dilution card has a low prior unless it uses within-coin timing (changes in issuance), matches on prior return, or sees unlock schedules.

title: Implied-over-realized volatility gives no usable relative signal across assets
statement: Three designs on the options-implied fear of assets have ended at the mechanism gate. A time-series equity tilt on the implied-over-realized ratio was right-signed but a near miss with too few episodes (H-0055). Short volatility timed by the implied curve was mostly the unconditional roll-down (H-0073, K-0088). New: ranking twelve ETFs across asset classes on the ratio against each asset's own year (H-0084) gave a wrong-signed average at every horizon from a week to a quarter, widening with horizon, positive only in the earliest third and worst in the latest. The reading is inferred, not tested: raw returns of the rich-ratio leg carry stress continuation and beta (K-0074), and any premium that exists is probably global and common to assets rather than asset-specific, which a relative ranking cancels. A further volatility-premium card on this family has a heavy trial count and a low prior unless it is a time-series design with many markets and an always-invested control.

title: Scout effect-size forecasts for slow cross-sectional cards ran far above what G1 measured in three cards
statement: H-0084, H-0085 and H-0087, all slow cross-sectional cards with a primary horizon of a quarter, forecast a side-adjusted gross of roughly one to a few percent per event, converted from published long-short spreads. G1 measured a wrong-signed average in two (H-0084, H-0085) and in the third (H-0087) a right-signed average at a small fraction of the low end of the forecast. The forecasts of event counts, dates and round-trip cost were close (events within a few percent of the forecast in H-0084 and H-0087; the cost of the liquid ETFs and perps as forecast), so K-0098 and K-0120 held; only the effect size was off. Related to K-0111: the forecast of the bar was reasonable, the forecast of the effect was not. A Scout who turns a literature spread into a per-event number should treat it as an upper bound (publication decay, long-short in a single vehicle, vol-scaling, unhedged currency and ETF tracking) and state what the card concludes if the effect is only a fraction of it.

title: G0 still passes no crypto_top_n universe on daily perp data (four cards)
statement: H-0076 and H-0085 both crashed their first G0 with data.universe None on binance_perp_1d, as H-0039 and H-0081 did earlier, so the gap has recurred in four cards over about three weeks. Each Builder wrote the same fallback (top n by trailing 30-day dollar volume), which may differ from the judge's definition, so the event sets may not be the judge's. In H-0076 the fallback then failed G0 seven more times on truncated look-ahead views of only 18 rows: a loop over the volume window assumed at least as many rows as the window, and the cohort shift had the same pattern. The Builder cites run numbers 188 to 263 for the crash and fixed it with min(window, rows). The card was DATA_READY on 2026-11-02 and IMPLEMENTED on 2026-11-03, so about a day was lost on top of the data wait. Rolling-window code must accept views shorter than its window, because G0 cuts can be that short. Suggested: the gate passes the card's declared crypto_top_n universe on daily perp data, and G0 reports which universe the strategy used. Question sent to the owner.

title: lab try cannot exercise a LIQ-500 card with a minimum-names floor: the synthetic universe has fewer than 50 members
statement: The Builder of H-0094 (first learned-model card, a book that needs at least 50 scored members a day) reports that the synthetic universe in lab try has fewer than 50 members per day, so the book is flat and the diagnostic has zero events. With the floor temporarily set to 5 the book reached full gross (mean exposure about 0.7) and the diagnostic gave 26,759 events, then the floor was restored to 50. On real data G0 counted 351,176 events and G1 measured 350,685 with no look-ahead failures in 25 and 11 cuts, so G0 on real data was again the first meaningful check. This is the fourth family of cards that lab try cannot exercise, after the 8-K flag (K-0082), weekly CFTC reports (K-0092) and spot-perp pairs (K-0106). Suggested: give the synthetic LIQ-500 market at least 60 members, or let lab try scale a minimum-names floor to the synthetic universe. Not tested here: whether the walk-forward model fit runs on synthetic data at all.

title: Return-sort effects in liquid US stocks stay below cost, also as a learned composite of three sub-cost effects
statement: Past-return sorts in liquid US stocks, with reversal and continuation signs and many conditioners, almost all gave effects far below round-trip cost or nothing (H-0007, H-0029, H-0030, H-0065, H-0069). The exception, the reversal before a predicted earnings release (H-0064), cleared cost but was wrong-signed in the latest third and its book was far weaker than its event study. New: H-0094 merged no-news reversal, attention give-back and earnings-reaction drift into one learned score. Entries beat same-stock placebos in every third, but gross stayed under cost and faded across thirds. Combining sub-cost effects came closer than single sorts without clearing cost; whether nonlinearity matters is untested because the linear baseline never ran. A new return-sort card should argue gross above cost for its own entries, name the latest-third sign as a kill condition and include the linear control.

title: Learned-model cards: a column set defined by the whole-view universe makes walk-forward scores depend on the future
statement: H-0095 failed G0 look-ahead on its first run (truncation at 4 of 11 cuts, perturbation at 8). Cause per the Builder: features, labels and walk_forward were restricted to columns that are ever a universe member over the whole view. That set depends on future membership, and gbm fits depend on the column layout, so scores on earlier rows changed when a stock joined later. Fix: run on all columns and mask non-members per row; a regression test with late entrants and late-starting event data now covers it. Rule for learned cards: no column, row or training-sample subset may be chosen with information from the end of the view (ever-member lists, full-period filters, survivors). The synthetic lab try market could not show this, only G0 on real data did. H-0096 passed G0 on its first run.

title: Learned-model cards: lab try cannot run them and the ridge control never runs
statement: Two gaps, now seen in three learned cards (H-0094, H-0095, H-0096). (1) lab try: besides the universe of fewer than 50 members (K-0132), H-0095 shows that the synthetic 8-K flag is too sparse to reach walk_forward's minimum training sample (zero events) and that synthetic dollar volume has no cross-sectional dispersion, so a volume z-score is NaN. The Builder exercised the model path only by temporarily densifying events and by a regression test. On real data G0 was again the first meaningful check (event counts at G0 and G1 agreed within a handful: 8587 vs 8587 for H-0095, 15582 vs 15577 for H-0096). (2) Each of the three cards names a linear ridge baseline as a falsification criterion, and each ended at the G1 mechanism test before it could run. H-0096 asked the Skeptic or Librarian to have it run; neither has a command for it. So whether nonlinearity pays is untested in all three, and a Scout cannot tell a wrong learner from wrong features. Suggested: G1 reports the ridge event gross and percentile next to the model's whenever the card names a ridge baseline; the synthetic market gets a dense 0/1 8-K flag and volume dispersion.

title: Learned models on earnings-release events: near miss, wrong sign, no nonlinearity shown
statement: Three learned cards used the same real 8-K release events and overlapping features. A model trained on all days with news, volume and volatility features (H-0094) stayed under cost. A model trained only on release reactions to pick the drifting ones (H-0095) cleared everything except the placebo percentile, with a right sign in every third, but did not visibly improve on the plain positive-reaction cut of H-0033, which cleared the bar with room (different event sets, so indicative). A model with a release-window flag and earnings-information features (H-0096) was wrong-signed against same-stock placebos in every third. None has a ridge comparison, so the failures may be the features, not the learner. This fits K-0083: at the release only the stock's own price move carried, and adding second variables (earnings change, volume, run-up, last reaction) did not add on top. Drift effects again looked weakest in the latest third (K-0060). A further learned card on the same release events has a low prior unless it brings a new information source, not a new learner; a gross per entry argued clearly above cost is needed in advance.

title: Learned date-level state and calendar interactions in liquid US stocks: no timing value in two designs
statement: Two learned cards gave a gradient-boosted score date-level inputs that are the same for every stock on a date, so that only an interaction could use them: month-turn and macro-release clocks with beta, volatility and liquidity (H-0098), and VIX and market-drawdown state with residual reversal, volatility and beta (H-0099). Both ended at the mechanism test with entries no better than same-stock placebos on shifted dates, in H-0098 clearly worse, and with gross far under round-trip cost. The placebo bars were under cost, so these are not power problems. Neither card could show whether the model split on the date inputs at all, because feature importance and the by-state split did not reach the gate. The reading is that liquid-stock selection does not become profitable by switching a static tilt with the calendar or the volatility state, and the month-turn fade of K-0038 and the weak reversal of K-0133 reappear in the learned form. A further card of this type has a low prior unless it reports how the model used the state.

title: A gbm-versus-ridge disagreement event runs the ridge control inside G1; first result is a small gain inside the cloud
statement: K-0135 found that the ridge baseline named by learned cards never ran. H-0100 solved it in the card design: the mechanism event was a release row where exactly one of two walk-forward models, gbm or ridge on the same features, rows and schedule, ranked the stock in its top fifth, with side plus one for gbm-only and minus one for ridge-only, so the placebo test asks whether nonlinearity pays. It worked in the framework (5268 events, G0 and G1 counts equal). Result: positive average, placebo mean near zero, percentile 0.90 against the 0.95 bar, gross about 0.59 of round-trip cost, bar under cost. The other three learned cards of this batch (H-0097, H-0098, H-0099) still did not get a ridge result. Limits of the design: both sides are mixed in one number, raw against unmarked peers (K-0074), and the event count depends on how much the two models overlap (counted about twice the Scout forecast). Cards that claim an interaction should use this design or ask for a ridge row in the G1 output.

title: Filing-anchored sorts pass twice in LIQ-500; a learned conditional form did not
statement: Two sorts with different content, net repurchasers against issuers (H-0019) and low against high quarterly accruals (H-0092), were both timed to the quarterly filing and held for a week in LIQ-500. Both cleared the same-stock placebo bar with gross above round-trip cost, and both books ended near T-bills (K-0064). They share filing dates, universe and seasons, so this is one piece of evidence seen twice. H-0019 faded era by era, H-0092 was positive in every third, and the effect in H-0092 was present in the first session and kept building. New: H-0097 added the release reaction and event time in a learned long-only form. Fresh-filer entries stayed inside the placebo cloud, gross was under cost, and the latest third was wrong-signed, so the claim that filing information is conditional on the headline reaction adds nothing visible over the plain accrual sort. The release-anchored sort (H-0027) and the slow style (H-0086) also failed, so the anchor matters and the pass may be filing-linked or early-era. A further filing card in LIQ-500 has a low prior; untested are the long leg alone, beta-matched legs and less covered stocks.

title: Scout effect-size forecasts ran above G1 in seven cards; counts and cost were close
statement: K-0130 named three slow cards (H-0084, H-0085, H-0087). Four learned five-session cards add the same pattern. Forecast gross per entry against measured: H-0097 15-30 bps against about 7; H-0098 10-25 against about zero; H-0099 5-12 against about 1; H-0100 more than 20 needed for a pass, about 7 measured. Event counts were at or above the forecast: 12354 against 6000-12000, 134177 against 70000-120000, 48759 against 30000-50000, and 5268 against about 2200-2800 in H-0100 (the overlap of two models was misjudged). Round trips matched for LIQ-500 (about 11 to 12 bps forecast and measured) but for LIQ-200 H-0099 forecast 6-7 bps and G1 used about 10; cause not read (possibly the fractional-quote era enters the mean). H-0100 forecast a placebo bar near 20 bps, measured about 8. A literature-derived or reasoned gross is still an upper bound; the Scout should state in the card what it concludes if the effect is a quarter of the forecast, and take the cost from the pooled dev period, not the current tier.

title: Learned release-event cards: a new information source, market attention load, did not help
statement: K-0136 said a learned card on real 8-K release events needed a new information source, not a new learner. H-0101 supplied one, the market-wide release load of the session and an end-of-week flag, next to the stock's own reaction. Entries earned about what the same stocks earn on shifted dates, with gross under round-trip cost, so the attention interaction added nothing to the drift the plain positive-reaction cut of H-0033 already shows. With H-0098 and H-0099 (K-0137) it is the third learned card whose date-level inputs gave no timing value in liquid US stocks. At the release only the stock's own price move has carried (K-0083); second variables have not added on top in H-0094, H-0095, H-0096, H-0100 or H-0101. Method note: the load rank needs a year of history and the walk-forward a training sample, so the first third of dev had no entries and the verdict rests on two blocks. The ridge control and the by-load split did not reach the gate; only H-0100 ran a ridge comparison. A further learned release-event card has a low prior unless it changes the stocks or reports the interaction directly.

title: Disagreement events against a ridge control: four cards, no nonlinear gain; G0 and G1 counts agree
statement: The design of K-0138 (mechanism event = picks or rows one model makes and the linear control does not, same features, rows, label and schedule) has now run in H-0100, H-0103 (a TCN against a ridge, both sides marked), H-0104 and H-0105. G0 and G1 event counts agreed within a handful (30603 and 30559, 15162 and 15158, 12349 and 12347), so the design works in the framework. Results: near the percentile bar with a bar under cost (H-0100), bottom of the cloud (H-0103), far under the bar (H-0104, H-0105). Two were wrong-signed (H-0103, H-0105), so there the disagreement set favoured the ridge side; the other two were positive but a small fraction of cost. The nonlinear form has not beaten its linear control in any of them, across three feature sets. Limits: the average mixes 'learner wrong' with 'control right' and the control's picks are never run as a book; the sign of a wrong-signed result is dev-selected, so the mirror is not a lead; event counts depend on model overlap and ran above forecast. A card that claims an interaction should still use this design and state what it concludes if the ridge side wins.

title: Learned earnings-reaction cards: ownership, event time and non-filed gaps added nothing
statement: K-0141 asked for a new information source or for the interaction to be reported directly. Both came in and failed. Institutional ownership with arbitrage risk (H-0102) gave entries below same-stock placebos, gross a fraction of cost and a slow-drift horizon shape. Event-time features of the latest reaction scored over all members (H-0104), tested as picks only the gbm makes against a ridge, were also below placebos and grew with horizon instead of fading. Overnight gaps with no filing and earnings windows excluded (H-0105) went wrong-signed against the ridge. With H-0095, H-0100 and H-0101, five learned cards in the reaction family have died on the mechanism test, and none beat the plain reaction rule of H-0033; the only near miss (H-0100) had a bar under cost. Second variables did not add at the release (K-0083), and a learned combination of them does not either. A further learned card on release reactions or overnight news in LIQ-500 has a low prior. Untested: other stocks (not loadable) and holds beyond a week argued from the slow build.

title: Scout gross-per-entry forecasts ran above G1 in eleven cards; round trips matched
statement: Four more learned cards, forecast gross per entry against measured: H-0102 15 to 30 bps against about 3; H-0104 10 to 25 against about 1; H-0103 3 to 8 against negative; H-0105 20 to 40 against negative. Each card wrote a 'quarter of the forecast' scenario (for example 4 to 8 bps for H-0102) as the pessimistic case, and in all four the measurement was below that case. With the seven cards of K-0140 that makes eleven. Event counts: H-0102 1957 against 1800 to 2300 (matched); H-0103 30559 against 15000 to 25000; H-0104 15158 against 3000 to 8000; H-0105 12347 against 1500 to 8000. The forecasts that counted the overlap of two models or a threshold on a tail variable ran low, as in K-0140. Round trips matched: LIQ-500 about 11 bps in H-0102, H-0104 and H-0105, LIQ-300 about 11 in H-0103. A Scout should take a literature gross as a ceiling, write the conclusion for a tenth of it as well, and forecast event counts from a dev-period count of the candidate condition.

title: G1 blocks are thirds of the whole dev period; an empty block cannot count, a thin one can
statement: H-0105 stated no data period. G1 reported 12347 events at about 540 per year, which implies about 23 years of denominator, i.e. the default dev start in 1998, while the 8-K flag starts in 2004, so its first block had zero events. mechanism_blocks appears to count blocks with a positive mean (H-0102 and H-0104 passed with two positive blocks of three, H-0103 and H-0105 scored zero), so an empty block can never count and the card needed both other blocks positive. Conversely H-0102 had 87 events in its first block, and that block counted as one of its two passing blocks, so a thin block can supply the pass. Both readings are inferred from the metrics, not from the code. Scouts should set the period start at the dataset's first usable date (8-K from 2004-09, 13F from mid-2013) so that the blocks are real. Suggested: report events by block at G0 and require a minimum event count per block before it counts.

title: Sector-ETF flow days: constituent reversal cleared the placebo and cost bars once, episodic and not isolated
statement: In one learned card (H-0106), stocks that newly entered the extreme legs of a model score on days when their assigned sector SPDR traded abnormal volume with an abnormal move earned a same-side abnormal return that beat time-shifted placebos of the same stocks and covered round-trip cost. The shape was a reversal that builds over a few sessions and fades by two weeks, and the latest third of dev was positive, unlike most short-horizon effects (K-0060). The middle third was about zero and the effect is clustered in stress days, so it looks episodic. This contrasts with date-level states (K-0137) and plain return sorts (K-0133) in the same universe, which found nothing, and fits K-0024 (mandated or non-fundamental flow events are the nearest live candidates in large caps). Caveats: one card; no control for large sector moves at normal wrapper volume, no ridge comparison, no split by side, and the sector legs carry a beta gap (K-0074), so a plain sector-reversal reading is not excluded. It did not become a strategy (see the method entry on rare-state books).

title: A rare-state mechanism that passes its event study cannot carry a daily learned book (H-0106)
statement: H-0106 is the first learned daily book whose mechanism test passed clearly: 5563 flow-day entries on 325 dates, placebo percentile 0.99, gross per entry about 28 bps against a round trip of about 13.5 bps. The book traded 124656 entries, so flow-day entries were about 4.5 percent of them. G1: gross Sharpe about 0.01, net about -0.76, long leg +0.22, short leg -0.61, cost drag about 4.7 percent a year. The other entries earned nothing and the short leg lost, as the card's own book arithmetic (K-0064) predicted. Rule: a rare-state mechanism needs an always-invested tilt or an event-slot book (K-0005, K-0027) with the expected annual gain written down. Forecast check (K-0144): event count and flow days were in range, gross per entry was above the central forecast, the first learned card not below its pessimistic case. Suggested for G1: report book gross for mechanism entries and for all others.

title: Sector-ETF flow days: the constituent reversal did not reproduce once market-wide stress was removed
statement: H-0106 found a reversal after sector-ETF flow days that beat placebos and covered cost (K-0146), but its sector moves were mostly market-wide. H-0107 removed that by construction: the push was the wrapper's move residual to SPY, stocks with an own filing that day were excluded, industry ETFs added flow days outside market stress. Entries were no better than same-stock placebos, gross was about half of cost, the first sessions were negative, ten sessions flat, and the thirds disagreed in sign. The placebo bar lay above cost, so a small effect was unresolved, but nothing suggests a hidden tradable one. The H-0106 pass most likely belonged to market-wide stress days (K-0084), not to wrapper-specific basket flow. The cards also differ in model, entry rule and side, so this is a lean, not a refutation. Untested: ordinary-day control, up-push side, ridge rule. A further ETF-flow card has a low prior without a stress control or ownership data.

title: Scout gross-per-entry forecasts ran above G1 in fourteen cards; event counts built from the condition arithmetic matched
statement: Three more learned cards. H-0108 forecast a central gross of about 20 bps per marked event, 5 at a quarter and 2 at a tenth; G1 measured about 3 (cost ratio about a quarter of an 11 bps round trip), below the quarter case. H-0109 forecast about 12 central and 5 pessimistic; measured about minus 4. H-0110 forecast 5 to 15 central and 1 to 3 at a tenth; measured about minus 2. With the eleven of K-0144 that makes fourteen, and the pessimistic case was beaten again in all three. Event counts matched this time: H-0108 forecast 40000 to 50000, counted 39268; H-0109 forecast 8000 to 10000, counted 9592; H-0110 forecast 4000 to 9000, counted 5014. Those counts came from a tail fraction times dates, or from a dated rule, unlike the overlap and threshold counts that ran low in K-0140 and K-0144. Round trips again matched (about 11 bps in LIQ-500). Rule for Scouts: derive counts from the condition arithmetic, treat a literature gross as a ceiling, and state what the card concludes if gross is a tenth of it or the sign is wrong.

title: Learned sign-split conditioners from new sources added no timing value in liquid US stocks
statement: Three more learned cards took a literature mechanism that predicts a sign split inside a set of liquid US stocks: value-anchored rebound after extreme non-earnings drops (H-0108), Miller overpricing before earnings releases (H-0109) and a one-year capital-gains clock after volume spikes (H-0110). None beat time-shifted placebos of the same stocks: two were wrong-signed, one positive but a small fraction of cost. Only for H-0109 did the placebo bar lie under cost, so the others leave a tiny effect unresolved. With K-0133, K-0137 and K-0143, fundamentals, ownership, attention, calendar state, disagreement proxies and tax clocks have each failed to lift a five-session large-cap sort above cost. The ridge control never ran at the gate, so nonlinearity is untested; the conditioners themselves show nothing at this horizon.

title: Scout gross-per-entry forecasts ran above G1 in fifteen cards; this time the event count also came in below the forecast
statement: H-0111 forecast a central gross of 12-18 bps per entry, about 4 at a quarter of that and 1-2 at a tenth, and a round trip of about 11 bps in LIQ-500. G1 measured about 2.4 bps gross (cost ratio about a fifth of an 11.2 bps round trip), between the quarter and tenth cases, so the pessimistic case was beaten again (fifteen cards with K-0149). The round trip matched. Unlike the three cards in K-0149, the event count missed: forecast 20000-27000 (25-35 entries on about 780 weekly dates), counted 15113 on 703 dates, about 21 per date. The tail-fraction arithmetic overstated entries per date, probably because the middle-range past-return filter and the previous-week entry rule overlap more than the independence arithmetic assumed (inferred, not tested), and fewer scored dates existed than forecast. Rule for Scouts: when an entry rule combines a tail entry with a second filter, count entries per date from a rough simulation of the actual overlap, not from the product of fractions, and keep the K-0149 advice to treat a literature gross as a ceiling and state what the card concludes at a tenth of it.

title: Return-distribution shape joins the learned conditioners that added nothing in liquid US stocks
statement: A fourth learned card on a literature mechanism in liquid US stocks over a week (after H-0108, H-0109, H-0110) used a new source: the shape of the recent return distribution (H-0111, skewness from overnight and intraday half-day returns). Tail entries were no better than the same stocks on shifted dates, gross was a small fraction of cost, the first third of dev was wrong-signed and the effect showed only at the longest horizon. The placebo bar lay below cost, so not a power problem. With K-0133, K-0137 and K-0143, no conditioner tried (fundamentals, ownership, attention, calendar, tax clock, distribution shape) lifted a one-week large-cap sort above cost. The ridge control never ran (K-0135). The half-day split is coarse, so the published intraday-skew effect is not refuted.

title: Core-plus-tilt books have no core-only control, so a margin over SPY cannot be attributed to the tilt
statement: H-0033 (positive-reaction tilt) and H-0113 (quarterly share-update tilt) are long-only books on a cap-weighted core with a tilt held a small part of the time, benchmarked against SPY total return. G1 reports no core-only run, no return of the tilt-window sleeve and no tracking of the core against SPY. In H-0113 G1 and G2 passed with a Sharpe margin over SPY far larger than its event study could supply: the event average was concentrated in the earliest third and about zero or negative in the middle third, yet the book beat the benchmark in every third; neighbors, an alternative universe and doubled costs all passed with the same Sharpe, and the random-entry null had a median Sharpe near zero for an always-invested book, which is odd (K-0078). The core is built from share counts times unadjusted close, with names leaving the index sent to cash, not from SPY, so the margin may come from core construction, a bug, or a window effect much larger than the events show. None of these is separated by the outputs. Suggested: G1 reports the core-only Sharpe and the window sleeve's return; the Builder reports the core's correlation with SPY. A question went to the owner.

title: First G3 verdict: DSR failed at the hurdle, and the family trial count seems to include grid points
statement: H-0113 is the first card to reach G3 and the first to fail it. The deflated Sharpe came out just above one half, with the per-period Sharpe about equal to the hurdle (hurdle above the benchmark's own Sharpe) and a probability of backtest overfitting a little above one half. The result lists 12 family trials where the family index-inclusion-price-pressure holds three gated hypotheses (H-0017, H-0022, H-0113) and one parked (H-0018); 12 fits three gated hypotheses plus the nine grid configurations of this card (3 x 3), but this is inferred, the code was not read. If grid points count as trials, a card with a full grid starts with nine and each earlier family member adds to the hurdle. A book whose Sharpe merely clears the hurdle gets a DSR near one half by construction, so G3 is decided by the margin over the hurdle, not by passing G1 and G2. Reusing a family on purpose (as the Scout did) is the honest choice and has this price. Open: how n_family_trials is counted, and whether the benchmark's Sharpe enters the hurdle.

title: A linear reversal score in the volatile half of liquid stocks cleared cost; nonlinear ones did not
statement: Past-return sorts and learned composites in liquid US stocks mostly stayed below cost (K-0133), and the linear baseline that K-0133 and H-0103 asked for had never run. It has now (H-0115): a ridge on recent intraday and overnight moves, the prior week's return, a volume shock and volatility, restricted to the high-volatility half of a liquid universe, gave weekly entries that beat same-stock placebos with a bar under cost, covered round-trip cost, kept the sign in every third and built over the first days before easing, the shape of a liquidity concession. The nonlinear versions on similar information did not: a gbm with news features stayed under cost (H-0094), a TCN on price paths was wrong-signed against the ridge (H-0103), a gbm-versus-ridge disagreement on flow days added nothing (H-0112). So far nonlinearity has hurt, not helped. Caveats: one card and one universe tier; the event average is raw against unmarked peers, and the book's short leg lost money, so market exposure of the volatile half is not excluded (K-0074); the net book missed the absolute floor on taker cost. Sorts outside the volatile half remain below cost.

title: An estimated stock-level oil link carried a delayed response, but it faded in the latest third
statement: Claims that news in one liquid market is priced late in another had come out flat or wrong-signed from daily to monthly horizons: statistical peer catch-up (H-0013), macro-release continuation (H-0047), oil against Treasuries (H-0056) and earnings news passed to peers (H-0066). K-0080 left explicit economic links untested. H-0114 used one: each stock's estimated oil exposure times the oil-specific move of the last two weeks. The pooled mechanism test passed, with entries above the placebo bar, gross above cost and a response that peaked within days and eased later, the first positive diffusion result of this kind. It was positive in the first two thirds of dev and wrong-signed in the latest third, and the book was invested a small part of the time, with a long leg that earned and a short leg that lost, so it missed the absolute floor. A stock-level link estimated from the stock's own history can therefore carry a delayed response that undated or statistical links did not, but it decays like other effects (K-0060) and rests on few oil episodes. Do not trade the mirror. Untested: the ridge control, an oil-up against oil-down split, an episode split.

title: Scout gross forecasts split in the latest four cards: below, central and above the range
statement: K-0151 found Scout forecasts of gross per entry above G1 in fifteen cards and advised treating a literature gross as a ceiling. The four cards decided on 2026-11-08 do not follow that pattern. H-0112 (index-basket pressure) came in below its pessimistic case. H-0114 (oil exposure) came in at its central forecast. H-0113 (quarterly share updates) came in above its range, but the mean is early-third heavy and does not reconcile with the book (see the framework entry on core-only controls). H-0115 (linear reversal baseline) came in above its optimistic case after a deliberately low central forecast. Event counts were inside or slightly above the forecast ranges in all four, and round trips matched except H-0113. Reading: the pessimistic case remains a useful floor and the gross is still usually far under cost for mechanism-from-literature cards, but cards built on a measured statistical regularity (a baseline, an exposure estimated from the stock's own history) can exceed forecasts. Four cards are too few to retune a rule; keep stating the forecast at a tenth of the central case.

title: Estimated-exposure diffusion in liquid US stocks: oil passed once, rate, dollar and credit news did not
statement: K-0156 read H-0114 as the first positive delayed-response result, driven by a stock-level link estimated from the stock's own history. H-0116 applied the same construction (estimated exposure times a market-residual shock, a gradient-boosted score, weekly legs, five-day hold) to ten-year Treasury yield, dollar and credit-spread news. Entries on the model's legs with an agreeing implied move earned a slightly negative abnormal return, in the middle of the same-stock placebo cloud and below cost, with only the earliest third positive and the latest the worst. Event and date counts were large, so the sign is informative. So the oil pass was not a general property of estimated macro exposures. Inferred, not tested: macro investors price rate, dollar and credit news quickly in futures, one year of daily regressions gives noisy betas for these factors, and oil has a direct large-cap link. The oil pass rests on few episodes and faded lately, so it may itself be episodic. Per-factor results and the ridge control were not reported. Do not file other macro prices on this construction without an argument for a direct, visible link.

title: Scout gross forecasts: the estimated-exposure card H-0116 came in below its pessimistic case
statement: K-0157 found that H-0112 fell below its pessimistic case, H-0114 matched its central case, and H-0113 and H-0115 exceeded their ranges, and suggested that cards built on a measured statistical regularity can beat forecasts. H-0116 (estimated factor exposure, same construction as H-0114) is a fifth data point and goes the other way: G1 counted 13071 events on 301 dates against a forecast of 14000-22000 events and 280-450 gate-on dates, so the count was slightly below range and the dates inside it; the round trip was about 11 bps against 12-15 forecast; but gross per event was negative against a central forecast of 15 bps and a pessimistic one of 1.5 bps. The Scout wrote the pessimistic case before the result, as asked, and it was still too high. Reading: an exposure-based card that reuses a mechanism that passed once (H-0114) cannot take that pass as the central case for new inputs. Five cards remain too few to retune a rule. Keep stating the forecast at a tenth of the central case and add the case in which the mechanism is absent.

title: The linear reversal score in the volatile half of liquid stocks did not reproduce when re-specified
statement: K-0155 read H-0115 as a clean liquidity concession: a ridge score in the high-volatility half of a liquid universe beat same-stock placebos, covered cost, kept its sign in every third and eased after the first week. H-0117 re-used the claim with the score rebuilt from the lesson text, new leg entries as the event, and a buffered, beta-neutral book as the change. Its entries stayed under the placebo percentile bar, gross per entry was under round-trip cost, a large share of the average was earned by the same stocks on shifted dates, the latest third was much weaker, and the effect grew toward the longest horizon instead of easing. The two cards differ in inputs, event definition and trial luck, so this is not a refutation of H-0115, and it is not a confirmation either. Reading: the volatile-half concession is, so far, one pass that did not repeat, with a market-exposure reading (K-0074) still open. Treat it as unconfirmed; the nonlinear failures of K-0155 stand. A further card on this score needs the exact H-0115 inputs, a beta-matched or volatile-versus-calm control, or a different information source.

title: Book-change cards are gated by an entry event study; base score may be a rebuild
statement: H-0117 was filed to test two book changes (a rank buffer and beta-neutral leg sizes) on a score that had passed in H-0115. Two things made that unanswerable. (1) G1 runs the mechanism test first and stops when it fails (strategy_not_run), but the mechanism test sees only new leg entries; continuing holdings, the buffer's purpose, and the leg sizing are visible only in the strategy run. A card whose claim is a book change therefore can die on a test that does not measure the change, and the card's own forecast named the absolute Sharpe floor as the likely death, not the event test. (2) The Scout states it did not see the exact H-0115 feature windows or alpha and rebuilt them from the lesson text, so 'same score, so the mechanism test reproduces a known pass' could not be checked and was not borne out. Suggested: when a card builds on an earlier pass, the Scout gets the earlier spec (features, windows, parameters), and a book-change card may state whether it wants the strategy run even if the entry test misses. Also: the registry code shows only the percentile failure while the cost check failed too (K-0069, K-0098).

title: Learned date-level state and calendar interactions in liquid US stocks: two nulls and one near miss at a legal deadline
statement: Two learned cards gave a gradient-boosted score date-level inputs that are the same for every stock on a date: month-turn and macro-release clocks (H-0098) and volatility and drawdown state (H-0099). Both ended with entries no better than same-stock placebos and gross far under cost. A third, the October and December tax-deadline clocks interacting with holders' loss state (H-0118), came closer: right-signed, placebo mean near zero, gross just above round-trip cost, percentile just under the bar, and a bar above cost, so a small real effect is not excluded. Unlike the usual decay (K-0060) its earliest third was wrong-signed and the later two positive, and the horizon profile was slow rather than a quick release. So the only date-level conditioner that did not read as null is a clock tied to a dated legal deadline, and that is one near miss on a part-time book. In none of the three could the model's use of the date inputs be seen. The reading of K-0137 stands for month-turn, macro-release and volatility states: switching a static tilt with them adds nothing. A further card of this type should report how the state was used, or be a tilt on an always-invested core.

title: An empty first G1 block also comes from model warm-up on short windows, and the registry hides it
statement: K-0145 explained an empty first block by a dataset starting after the default dev start (8-K flag from 2004). H-0120 shows a second cause. It was a crypto learned card on 2020-2022 with a refit every 63 rows: G1 counted 0, 165 and 336 events in the three blocks, mechanism_blocks was 1 against a minimum of 2, with only the latest block positive. The first fit needs a minimum training sample, so the first third of a three-year window holds no scored entries. This fits the reading of K-0145 that an empty block cannot count, so a short-window learned card needs both later blocks positive; the Scout foresaw it in the card. The registry shows only the percentile code, although the block and cost checks also failed (K-0069, K-0098). Scouts of learned cards on windows of about three years should state which block will be empty and expect the block check to bind; suggested: report events per block at G0 and list every failing check in the registry reason.

title: Estimated-exposure diffusion: oil passed once; rates, dollar, credit and non-oil commodities did not
statement: K-0158 read the oil pass of H-0114 against the failure of H-0116 on rate, dollar and credit news, and left open whether direct economic links in other commodities would repeat it. H-0119 tested that on gold, natural gas, grains and base metals, taken net of the stock market and of oil, with the same construction (estimated exposure times a residual shock, a gradient-boosted score, weekly legs, five-day hold). Entries earned about zero, below the same-stock placebo mean, gross a small fraction of cost, event and date counts ample. So the oil pass is not a general property of direct producer and user links; it is either specific to oil, where the link to large caps is big and visible, or episodic, as its faded latest third suggested. Inferred, not tested: ETF proxies for gas, grains and metals are noisy shock measures, and one year of daily regressions gives noisy exposures for stocks with weak links. Per-commodity results and the ridge control were not reported. Do not file further prices on this construction without an argument for why the shock series is clean and the link large.

title: Events defined as a subset of a model's own calls ran an order of magnitude below the Scout's count; cost matched
statement: H-0121 marked only the gbm's continuation calls (new entries to a leg whose recent move agrees with the leg side). The card forecast about 4000 to 8000 events; G0 and G1 both counted 547 on 280 dates (about 34 a year), so roughly a tenth of the lower bound. The Scout had written that a model that never calls continuation would fail the event count, but still built the forecast from condition arithmetic: a quarter to a half of leg names. The round trip matched (about 11 bps forecast, 11.4 modelled); gross per event came in near 1.6 bps against a central forecast of 15 bps. K-0142 saw model-defined event counts run above forecast, so the direction is not systematic; the point is that such counts cannot be derived from conditions alone. A card with model-defined events should give a count range from a stated call rate, say what the card concludes at a call rate a tenth of that, and note that the G1 minimum of 200 events and 2 positive blocks may bind. The registry again shows only the percentile code while the cost check failed too (K-0069, K-0098).

title: Information-asymmetry markers add nothing for a learned large-cap sort; continuation calls were rare
statement: K-0152 listed fundamentals, ownership, attention, calendar, tax clock and return-distribution shape as learned conditioners that did not lift a one-week large-cap sort above cost. H-0121 adds a fifth source from the literature on informed versus hedging volume: R&D intensity, how much news past releases revealed, and position in the earnings cycle, on non-earnings weeks with a volume-accompanied move. Only the model's continuation calls were marked, because no reversal rule can make them. They were rare relative to the card's expectation (inferred: the model mostly faded moves), averaged about zero against same-stock placebos, and gross was a small fraction of cost. The thirds disagreed in sign and the latest was the best, so this is not the usual decay (K-0060) but not a stable effect either. The placebo bar lay above cost, so a large effect was excluded and a modest one was not. The ridge control and the low-versus-high asymmetry split never ran (K-0135). In large caps the sign flip of the volume-return relation with information asymmetry is not visible with these markers, and a further learned conditioner has a low prior.

title: H-0113 core-only control: the reconstructed S&P 500 core beats SPY_TR by 7.9 %/yr on dev; the model window adds nothing
statement: Dev 1998-2020 (holdout unread): full book Sharpe 0.744 / CAGR 16.8 %, core only (same code, empty window, no LightGBM) 0.740 / 16.5 %, SPY_TR 0.390 / 8.0 %. Full minus core +0.24 %/yr (t 0.35); core minus SPY_TR +7.9 %/yr (t 4.4), same sign in all three thirds. The margin over the benchmark in G1-G3 belongs to the core, not to the signal. A cap-weighted S&P 500 rebuilt from members and sharesbas x close_u should track SPY_TR, so the core itself is suspect (membership, delists, share counts, splits); not yet traced. Cards of the form core plus a short model window need a core-only control.

title: sharesbas is split-adjusted to today, close_u is not: shares x close_u overweights later splitters (H-0113)
statement: H-0113 built its S&P 500 core from sf1_arq_sharesbas x close_u. In 2010 that gives a total cap of 24.9 tn USD (real ~6 tn) and a top-10 weight of 60 % (real ~20 %): Apple 2010 = 25.5 bn shares (after the later 7:1 and 4:1 splits) x 251 USD (before them). Names that split later, the later winners, are overweighted, so the weights carry future information. A split-consistent core (shares x split-adjusted price anchored at the last close) gives 8.2 %/yr vs SPY_TR 7.95 % on dev 1998-2020 (diff -0.3 %/yr, t -0.3); the raw core gives 15.5 % (diff +7.4 %/yr, t 4.2). The whole G1-G3 margin of H-0113 was this mismatch; the model window added +0.24 %/yr (t 0.35). The framework look-ahead test cannot see it: the share counts are in the dataset as stored. Other cards use sf1_*_marketcap (point-in-time at filing), and H-0033 anchors marketcap and grows it by total return; none multiplies sharesbas by close_u. Rule for Builder: never build market cap as sharesbas x close_u; use sf1_*_marketcap anchored at its last change and grown by total return, or an equivalent split-consistent price.
evidence: ["H-0113 g3_dsr 2026-11-08","scratchpad core/core_diag.py (dev rows only, holdout unread)"]

title: Learned large-cap sorts: the dollar price grid and macro-cleaned residuals add nothing either
statement: K-0166 listed fundamentals, ownership, attention, calendar, tax clock, return-distribution shape and information-asymmetry markers as learned conditioners that did not lift a short-horizon large-cap sort above cost. Two more sources failed. H-0122 used the price level on the dollar grid (next-session hold, picks only a gbm makes against a ridge): entries beat peers slightly, but a sizeable share was earned by the same stocks on shifted dates, gross was a small fraction of cost, and the effect was largest early and grew with the horizon. H-0123 split the weekly move into a cross-asset part and a residual for a ridge: entries matched placebos, gross was near zero, and the thirds disagreed. In both the placebo bar lay below cost, so not a power problem. In the most liquid stocks neither a behavioral microstructure input nor a cross-asset input brings gross near a taker's round trip. Any grid effect probably sits in low-priced names or needs resting orders. A further learned conditioner has a low prior.

title: Zero events pass G0 and read as a mechanism failure: a learned crypto card that probably never scored
statement: K-0062 listed three cards that ended on the event count without a mechanism result (H-0021, H-0038, H-0043). H-0124 is a fourth, and the first learned one: G0 passed with zero events in dev and a runtime of 0.19 s, while learned cards of the same days took 264 s (H-0122) and 85 s (H-0123), so no walk-forward fit seems to have run. G1 then counted zero events and blocks; the registry shows g1_mechanism_events, which reads as sparsity (K-0069). The card forecast about 1500 to 2500 events; H-0120, a learned card on the same kind of universe and window, did produce events, so warm-up alone does not explain it. Candidate causes, none verified: the all-valid sixty-day return rule including BTC, the VIX input with leading NaN, the minimum training sample against a three-year window, the universe the gate hands over (K-0131).
