Suggested: G0 flags zero events when hundreds are forecast and reports scored rows by year. A question went to the owner.

title: Scout forecasts: round trip and counts held; gross per entry fell below the central case in two more cards
statement: H-0122 forecast 80000 to 180000 events and a round trip near 11 bps; G1 counted about 180000 and 11.3 bps. Gross per entry was about 1.3 bps against a central 3 and an optimistic 12. The card named its likeliest death correctly (a real but sub-cost effect). H-0123 forecast 90000 to 100000 events and 10 to 12 bps; G1 counted about 75000 and 11.3 bps, with gross about 0.4 bps against a central 15 and a pessimistic 3, so below the pessimistic case; its likeliest death (mechanism passes, book misses the Sharpe floor) was wrong, the mechanism itself failed. Pattern with H-0116 and H-0117: a card that takes an earlier unconfirmed pass (H-0115, K-0160) as its central case has been too high each time. Keep writing the case in which the mechanism is absent. This supersedes K-0159.

title: Learned dollar-neutral books: the long leg earns and the short leg loses in four cards, also with beta-balanced legs
statement: In four learned dollar-neutral or beta-neutral weekly books whose event test passed, the G1 decomposition shows a positive long leg and a negative short leg: H-0106 (K-0147), H-0114, H-0115 and H-0126. The earlier reading for the first three was market exposure or a sector tilt (K-0074). H-0126 weakens that reading: its legs were built inside beta terciles and balanced by construction, and the short leg still lost. So the pooled event average (side-adjusted, against raw unmarked peers) probably leans on the long side, and the book pays for a short leg that adds cost and no return. The event study reports no side split, and the card of H-0126 named none, so this is inferred from leg Sharpes, not tested. A Scout writing a learned neutral card should state what it expects from each leg, and a Builder or G1 should report the event average by side. A long-only tilt on an always-invested core avoids the short leg but keeps the limits of K-0064 and K-0153.

title: Estimated-exposure diffusion: oil and credit passed the event test; rates, dollar and non-oil commodities did not
statement: K-0164 read the oil pass of H-0114 against nulls in rates, dollar, credit and non-oil commodities and called oil special or episodic. H-0126 corrects the credit part: the shock was the credit spread move not explained by stocks or Treasuries (market-based), and stocks were mapped by balance sheet (leverage, coverage, volatility), not by a return beta. Entries beat same-stock placebos, gross covered cost, and the sign held in every third, the latest included, unlike oil. H-0116 failed on credit with statistical betas, so the mapping probably decided, not the price. Both passes share a structural link and a clean shock; both books were part-time, missed the absolute Sharpe floor and had a losing short leg. Open: the ridge control never ran, the effect grew to the longest horizon (slow leverage drift not excluded), and the beta gap against unmarked peers was not neutralized (K-0074). Rates, dollar and non-oil commodities stay unsupported. A further card needs an explicit link and a clean shock series, not a new price.

title: H-0127 supports the three-peer rule as the cause of H-0038's empty G1 event set
statement: K-0086 inferred that G1 needs at least three unmarked peers per date (H-0041, H-0072) and K-0054 listed it as one possible cause of H-0038, whose universe held only TLT and SHY: G0 counted 241 events, G1 counted none. H-0127 filed the same Treasury auction cycle with five unmarked short-Treasury ETFs and a start date after the third peer lists. G0 counted 404 events and G1 measured 404, all with controls, so the mechanism was measured for the first time and the verdict is a measured negative. This supports the peer rule as the cause for H-0038 (inferred; gate code not read) and shows that G0 and G1 counts agree when peers exist from the start of the window. Still true from H-0072: when peers list late, G0 counts more events than G1. A card that marks every instrument it names, or leaves fewer than three unmarked, will read as zero events at G1 although G0 passed. Scouts should list the peers and the first date with three unmarked.

title: lab try cannot exercise two more data types: the Treasury auction calendar keys and the deposits field
statement: Same gap as K-0082 (8-K flag), K-0092 (CFTC weekly reports) and K-0106 (perp and spot pairs). The Builder of H-0127 reports that the synthetic treasury_auctions_1d series never hit the exact integer session counts the card tests (next_coupon5_sessions equal to four, last_coupon5_sessions equal to zero), so lab try showed zero events and zero trades; the logic was tested on hand-made calendars (lead, cluster rules, overlap, missing price, each hold). The Builder of H-0129 reports that every synthetic stock has deposits above zero, so the card's bank exclusion removed all of them and lab try showed zero trades; it ran once with the filter off and passed G0 with 25 cuts and 3099 entries. On real data G0 then reported events (404 for H-0127, 42242 for H-0129) and no look-ahead failures, and G1 counted nearly the same, so G0 on real data was again the first meaningful check. Suggested: give the synthetic auction calendar integer countdowns and make deposits missing for most synthetic stocks.

title: Macro-news diffusion into stocks: a plain credit rule and an inflation sort failed
statement: K-0173 read the credit pass of H-0126 as support for an explicit balance-sheet link plus a clean shock series. Two cards built exactly that and failed. H-0128 replaced the learned model with a plain leverage sort on the same credit-specific shock: right-signed but inside the placebo cloud, gross far under cost, wrong-signed in the earliest third, growing toward the longest horizon like slow style drift. H-0129 used a clean inflation-expectations shock and the nominal-versus-real asset split: inside the cloud, peaking in the first sessions and negative at longer horizons, not a build over the week. In both the placebo bar lay under cost. So the H-0126 pass is one result its linear control did not repeat: it needed the model's coverage and volatility inputs or was luck; the ridge control never ran. Oil (H-0114) is the only other pair that passed, once, with a wrong-signed latest third. Rates, dollar and non-oil commodities stay unsupported. A link and a clean shock are not sufficient; the prior for another card is low.

title: Scout forecasts: a calendar-key event count ran to a third of the forecast; gross short again
statement: K-0171 found counts and round trips holding while gross fell short of the central case, worst for cards that took an unconfirmed pass as central. Three more cards. H-0127 forecast 1100 to 1300 events and a 2 to 6 bps round trip; G1 counted 404 events on 202 dates and a 10 bps round trip, with negative gross against a pessimistic 3 bps. The count cause is unverified; the exact-lead and first-of-cluster rules probably cut it (inferred). H-0128, built on the H-0126 pass, forecast 40000 to 55000 events and 11 to 12 bps; G1 counted 55526 and about 12 bps, gross about 2.5 bps against a central 15 and a pessimistic 3. H-0129 forecast 37000 to 48000 events and 11 bps; G1 counted 42233 and about 11 bps, gross about 2.6 bps between pessimistic 0 and central 10; its likeliest death and its horizon-shape kill condition were right. Counts of shock-gated books and round trips are forecast well; calendar-key counts need exact key arithmetic; gross is too high when resting on an unconfirmed pass. Registry codes again hide the failed cost check (K-0069, K-0098).

title: A learned crypto card with a VIX input did score: warm-up and VIX leading NaN no longer explain H-0124's zero events
statement: K-0170 read H-0124 (learned crypto perps card, VIX and BTC-trend state) as probably never scored: G0 passed with zero events in 0.19 s and G1 counted none. H-0130 (learned crypto spot card, top twenty pairs, 2018-2022, six features each needing at most sixty days, VIX and 10-year real yield as raw date-level inputs, walk-forward refit every 63 rows) passed G0 with 554 events in about 12 s, and G1 counted the same 554 events on 118 dates, all with controls. Its first third of dev held no events (model warm-up, K-0163), the later two had 88 and 466. So a leading NaN in the VIX series and the minimum training sample are not sufficient causes for H-0124. The Builder's safeguards worked here: date-level features fed raw rather than through the cross-sectional z-score helper, coin features needing at least 45 of 60 pairs rather than all sixty, and non-members masked per row (K-0134). Candidates left for H-0124 (none verified): the perp universe the gate hands over, the all-valid sixty-day return rule, the BTC-trend feature. Also new: the card asked for event averages split by risk-off, risk-on and calm dates, and G1 reported none of them (K-0069).

title: US risk-state inputs do not visibly re-order the crypto cross-section over days
statement: Three cards conditioned a crypto coin sort on a TradFi state. A VIX-gated reversal in perps (H-0081) was inside the placebo cloud and below cost. A learned sort on beta, idiosyncratic risk and liquidity crossed with VIX and real-yield shifts (H-0130), tested as the picks only the gbm makes against a ridge on the same features, was positive on the point estimate but inside the cloud, below cost, flat or negative at one and ten days, with almost all of the gain in one third of dev and about nothing in the latest. The third, a VIX-switched momentum card (H-0124), never produced a score. So the flight-to-quality ladder story (levered altcoin holders de-risking with a lag after a US shock) found no usable ordering at the daily to weekly scale, and nonlinear state-by-characteristic interactions added nothing over the linear control, as in liquid US stocks (K-0162). Caveats: one boom-and-bust window, events on few dates, the sign flip between risk-off and risk-on was never reported, and the beta gap between picks is not neutralised (K-0074). Not tested: slower horizons, BTC alone as the traded asset, funding or stablecoin data as the transmission channel.

title: Stock-bond flow: a rally-side control did not reproduce the H-0046 pass
statement: H-0046 passed the event study on band-breach days of both directions, so stress rebound could not be separated from rebalancer flow (K-0068). H-0050 (quiet trigger) was slightly wrong-signed. New: H-0131 kept only the rally side, where no stress rebound exists. Equities lagged bonds, above a negative placebo mean (equity premium) but inside the placebo cloud, gross about equal to cost, latest third reversed, and the effect grew with horizon out to weeks: slow drift, not a week-long concession. Two different controls now fail to reproduce the pass, so the reading that H-0046 caught generic reversal after large spread moves and stress rebound (K-0084) is stronger. Still a lean: triggers differ, the H-0131 placebo bar lay above cost, H-0050 was thin. Four equity ETFs share dates, so independent evidence is the event dates. A further daily-ETF mechanical-flow card has a low prior unless the flow is seen where it trades.

title: H-0131 forecasts: events under the low end, ETF round trip about twice the card's
statement: H-0131 forecast 220-350 event dates, 900-1400 marked events and a 2-6 bps ETF round trip. G1 counted 135 dates, 540 events (about 29 per year, 4 marked ETFs per date) and a 10 bps round trip, the same ETF tier gap as H-0127 (K-0177) and the perp gap of H-0081 (K-0120). The rally state fired on about 3 percent of sessions against a forecast of 5-8 (inferred, not in a G0 output). Gross landed between the pessimistic and central cases, below central, as in K-0171 and K-0177. The card did name its likeliest deaths (placebo cloud, negative latest third) and used the negative placebo mean as a harder bar. Scouts should take the daily-ETF round trip from the gate's cost tier (about 10 bps), count state days from the real series after warm-up, and lead with the pessimistic case when the premise is an unconfirmed pass.

title: Disagreement events against a ridge control: six cards, no nonlinear gain, now also in crypto perps
statement: The design of K-0138 and K-0142 (event = picks only the model makes against the linear control) has now run in six cards: H-0100, H-0103, H-0104, H-0105, H-0130 and H-0134. H-0134 is the first on a monthly horizon in perps. Its gbm-only picks did worse than the ridge-only picks at every horizon, below the placebo mean, with the sign set by the cycle (clearly negative in the 2021 block, slightly positive in 2022) and an empty first block from warm-up (K-0163). Three of the six are wrong-signed (H-0103, H-0105, H-0134), the rest positive but inside the cloud or far under cost; none beat its linear control. G0 counted a few percent more events than G1 (793 and 767), as in K-0095, on only 77 weekly dates, so the event count can pass while the independent sample is small. The ridge side was never run as a book, so a wrong-signed result does not say the linear score pays, and its sign is dev-selected. Crypto momentum itself remains unscored in the lab (H-0124 never scored). A new learned card should state what it concludes if the ridge side wins and ask for the linear form as the primary claim.

title: Wrapper-gap reversion needs a cut arbitrage link
statement: K-0105 read ETF gaps as not reverting. H-0133 qualifies it. Fading a country ETF's US-hours move while its home exchange had a scheduled holiday cleared the placebo bar at the top of the cloud, with gross above event-leg cost, a positive sign in every third of dev, and a horizon profile that fit the claim: little on the first session, most once the home market reopened, less after a week. Together with closed-end funds against an ETF anchor (K-0103), the pattern is that wrapper deviations revert where creation and redemption cannot arbitrage them, and not for ordinary-day ETF gaps against factor proxies or twin ETFs (H-0037, H-0080), where the correction happens overnight in the home session. Neither pass became a strategy: the thinly traded wrappers and the hedge round trip took the margin, exposure was part-time, and the short side lost. The effect was much weaker in the latest third (K-0060), the comparison is against raw peers (K-0074), and it is one pass. A further wrapper card needs a link that is cut, not just a gap.

title: Nearness to the 52-week high has no timing content in three settings: it picks persistent winners
statement: Three anchoring cards died at the mechanism gate: stale-high breakouts in liquid US stocks (H-0011), nearness to the high within return-by-volatility cells (H-0083), and liquid crypto spot coins nearest their one-year high (H-0135). In H-0011 and H-0135 the raw gap was positive and above cost, but same-name placebos on shifted dates earned the same, so the sort selects names that do well in any week. In H-0135 the effect was largest early and nearly gone in the latest block, and grew with the horizon like the placebo. Reading: nearness to the high marks past winners; any premium is momentum or coin identity. Untested: crypto matched on prior return, and a dated own-price event conditioned on distance to the high. A further plain near-high card has a low prior.

title: Earnings-reaction drift in liquid US stocks lives in the first weeks; held a quarter it matches same-stock placebos
statement: On real 8-K dates a large positive reaction cleared the same-stock placebo over the first week in three designs (H-0028, H-0031, H-0033). H-0136 held the same kind of events to the next release. The abnormal return stayed positive, above cost, positive in every third with the latest among the strongest, and grew with horizon. But placebos of the same stocks on shifted dates earned more on average, so beyond the first weeks the set marks stocks that do well in any quarter (repeat positive reactors, persistent winners; K-0025, K-0184). This answers the open item of K-0143 (holds beyond a week) with a negative, and it is not the later-year large-cap decay of the literature, since the latest third did not weaken. Caveats: raw peers (K-0074); confirming releases of held stocks overlap; the book was never run. A longer-hold card on the plain rule has a low prior; only a control matched on reaction history could separate timing from identity.

title: Intraday cards: owner controls and mechanism claims outside the judge never run when G1 fails
statement: The intraday judge has no mechanism channel (no event study, no placebo, no side split). H-0137 put its decisive mechanism test, the same rule anchored at UTC midnight, and its long/short split outside the grid as a manual run by the Chair or owner. G1 rejected the card on net Sharpe, so seven falsification criteria, among them the US-open control and the bull-artefact check, were left unevaluated and the result says nothing about the mechanism. The same gap left H-0089 without its absorbed-versus-flow control. For intraday cards, a mechanism control that matters should be a grid dimension the judge reports (an anchor switch inside the grid, side as a parameter), or the card should accept that a G1 failure answers only the strategy question. Two cards, so confidence is low. Also: the Builder could not import zoneinfo and used hand-coded US daylight-saving rules with unit tests at the 2020 and 2021 transitions, a safe workaround that a card should not depend on silently.

title: 15m crypto perp taker rules held for hours: gross at or below cost
statement: Three kinds of trigger on fifteen-minute Binance perps, entered at the next open as a taker and held for hours, have now met the round-trip cost. Taker-dominated fast moves (rebound H-0035, continuation from compressed ranges H-0063) left a small positive average that a one-candle later fill or doubled costs erased (K-0077). New: a trigger not defined by flow, the first close beyond the opening range of the US cash session held to the US close (H-0137), also earned a gross a little under the round trip, with plenty of trades, so it is not a power problem. A long hold does not cure the cost problem for a taker. This agrees with study 16 (opening-range rule rejected on the holdout) and mrel-1h. The US-open specificity was never measured, so nothing is said about whether a clock-anchored flow exists, only that this taker rule does not harvest it in the dev window, one boom-and-bust cycle (K-0006). Cards on this time scale should state expected gross per trade against the round trip, after a one-candle delay, before filing.

title: 'Exactly the sibling's rule' cannot be verified: the Builder has no sibling code and G1 does not report gross per trade
statement: H-0138 was specified as H-0137's rule plus one filter, with the instruction that H-0137's implementation wins if it differs from the card text and that deviations be reported. The Builder reported that H-0137's code was not in its workspace and built from the card text, so the claim of an identical rule rests on the text alone (one ambiguity was also noted: the volatility rank window counted the last sessions with valid data, which equals the card text only with complete data). The card's owner criterion compares the mean gross trade of the filtered rule with the unfiltered sibling, but the G1 result carries mean net trade and cost share of gross, not gross per trade or per side; the Librarian had to derive it, and H-0137's own gross is known only from its lesson. Suggested: give the Builder the sibling's code for cards that declare 'same rule plus one condition', and add gross per trade and the long/short split to the G1 metrics for intraday cards, where there is no mechanism channel (K-0186).

title: 15m crypto perp taker rules held for hours: gross at or below cost; a volatility filter lowered it
statement: Fifteen-minute Binance perp triggers entered at the next open as a taker and held for hours have met the round-trip cost three ways: taker-dominated fast moves (H-0035, H-0063; erased by a later fill or doubled costs, K-0077), and the first close beyond the US-open range held to the US close (H-0137, gross a little under the round trip). New: H-0138 traded that rule only in the top third of trailing volatility, arguing trend days cluster there and fixed costs shrink against larger moves. Gross per trade came out far below the all-sessions rule's and the average trade lost clearly, so neither part held in dev. Long holds and volatility filters do not cure taker cost. This agrees with study 16 and mrel-1h. US-open specificity, the bottom-volatility run and the side split were never measured. Dev is one boom-and-bust cycle (K-0006). State expected gross per trade against the round trip, after a one-candle delay, before filing.

title: 15m crypto perp taker rules: only the US-open breakout after a narrow-range day cleared cost, fragile
statement: Fifteen-minute perp triggers entered as a taker and held for hours met round-trip cost in the earlier designs: fast taker-dominated moves (H-0035, H-0063), the all-sessions US-open breakout (H-0137, gross a little under the round trip) and its high-volatility subset (H-0138, worse). New: H-0139 traded the same breakout only after a narrow-range weekday and cleared G1 with gross above the round trip, surviving delay and doubled costs. It failed G2 narrowly on neighbor stability (longer window much weaker, fewer trades) and block concentration, the latest block carrying most of the return, the reverse of K-0060. Read with H-0138, volatility ordered gross as contraction-before-expansion predicts, but that is a hindsight comparison, not a tested dose response. The mechanism diagnostic never ran, so luck among the family's trials, the 2020-2021 drift and a 2022 short episode stay open (K-0006). Any further conditioner is a new trial counted with H-0137, H-0138 and study 16.

title: Intraday cards: owner diagnostics never run, after a G1 failure or a G1 pass
statement: The intraday judge has no mechanism channel (no event study, placebo or side split). K-0186 recorded two cards (H-0137, H-0089) whose decisive control was left unrun because G1 rejected them. H-0139 passed G1 and died at G2, yet its owner criterion (post-contraction versus other session move) and bull-artefact check (long versus short gross) were still not evaluated: the Builder wrote the diagnostic as a separate module that lab try neither runs nor scans, so it is untested until the Chair runs it by hand. Gate output still has no gross per trade or side split (K-0188); gross was derived from mean net trade and cost share. The card's own forecast said the longer-window neighbor would have too few trades, and that neighbor decided the G2 neighbor check. Suggested: judge-reported side and anchor split for every intraday card that reaches G2, and a flag for G2 neighbors below the minimum trades.

title: 15m crypto perp taker rules: of four US-open breakout conditioners only the narrow-range one cleared cost, fragile
statement: Fifteen-minute perp triggers entered as a taker and held for hours met round-trip cost only once. Fast taker-dominated moves (H-0035, H-0063), the all-sessions US-open breakout (H-0137, gross a little under the round trip) and its high-volatility subset (H-0138, worse) failed. H-0139, the breakout after a narrow-range weekday, cleared G1 with gross above the round trip and survived delay and doubled costs, then failed G2 narrowly on neighbor stability and block concentration (latest block strongest, the reverse of K-0060). New: H-0140 kept only breakouts agreeing with the move from UTC midnight to the US open; gross stayed near the unconditional rule, under cost, so the alignment filter thinned trades without selecting better ones. Only contraction ordered gross as expected, a hindsight comparison, not a dose response. No against-move control, side split or thirds ever ran in this family, so luck, the 2020-2021 drift and a 2022 short episode stay open (K-0006). Any further conditioner is a new trial counted with H-0137 to H-0140 and study 16.

title: Intraday cards: a control built into strategy.py as a parameter still does not run; four cards, no mechanism evidence
statement: K-0191: owner diagnostics written as separate modules are never run, and the intraday judge reports no side split or gross per trade. H-0140 took the other route: the pre-registered control was a side_mode argument (with, against, all) in the strategy function, same code path, to be run by the Builder or Chair. G1 judged only the primary run and rejected the card, so the against and all runs, side split and thirds were again not produced: a control exists only if the judge executes it. Gross per trade was again derivable only from mean net trade and cost share. The Builder had no timezone database and hand-coded the US daylight-saving rule (tested on March and November dates), and its 'all' mode still required a valid pre-session scale, so it is not exactly H-0137's trade set. Four cards (H-0137 to H-0140) have left no judge-produced evidence on side, anchor or control. Suggested: a judge-run controls list for intraday cards (named argument values run on dev, reporting trades, gross and net per trade, side split, thirds), counted as part of the card's trial, and gross per trade in the G1 metrics.

title: 15m crypto perp taker rules at the US open: coin-specific volume selection in alts did not lift the breakout above cost
statement: K-0192 found that of four breakout conditioners on BTC and ETH only a narrow-range one cleared round-trip cost, and that fragilely. H-0142 changed the cross-section instead of the state: only liquid alts with a coin-specific opening-volume shock, both sides, exit at the US close. It was worse than the unselected BTC/ETH rule. Derived gross per trade was near zero against a round trip that is larger for alts, trades were plentiful, the bootstrap bound of the mean net trade was below zero and drawdown was deep with little exposure. So the idea that a breakout carries information only when the coin has its own news did not transfer from stocks to crypto at taker cost in 2020-2022; the three variants that used a market-wide state or selection (volatility, alignment, coin volume) all failed and only contraction came close. A selection that picks high-volume alts probably picks high-beta flow in a factor-driven market. Unmeasured: the no-filter and lowest-volume controls, side split and thirds, because the judge does not run them (K-0193); and the maker route and holds longer than a session.

title: Cross-sectional sorts of ETFs on past returns: three designs, none clearly above same-ETF placebos
statement: Monthly-formation sorts of country and asset-class ETFs have now ended at the mechanism test three times without a clear gap over the same ETFs on shifted dates: country long-term reversal (H-0060, wrong-signed), bond-to-equity cross-asset momentum (H-0087, small and right-signed but inside the cloud, latest third negative) and, new, a learned frog-in-the-pan momentum score ranking ETFs inside fixed risk and defensive sleeves (H-0143). In H-0143 the average was tiny, over half of it was earned by the same ETFs on shifted dates, the thirds were unstable, and the effect peaked near one month and turned negative at a quarter. That is not the slow build and early-era weight of stock residual momentum (H-0054, a near miss). Reading, inferred: a cross-section of a few dozen ETFs gives few independent picks per date and a wide placebo cloud, and any in-sleeve momentum is small next to ETF round-trip cost. Plain in-sleeve momentum was never run as a control, so a path-shape conditioner was tested without knowing whether its base effect exists. A further ETF momentum card has a low prior unless it argues a horizon of about a month or less, or reports the plain sort first.

title: Crypto spot trend sorts: near-high and a learned life-cycle score both fail the same-coin placebo
statement: Two cards sorted liquid Binance spot coins on past trend and died at the mechanism test alike. Nearness to the one-year high (H-0135) was positive but no better than the same coins on shifted dates. A learned two-month score on six-month trend, run stage and volume trend (H-0144) was below its placebo, flat at short horizons, and wrong-signed in both later thirds, boom era included. The placebo mean was positive in both, so the sort picks coin identity, not timing. With K-0128 and study 9, no coin-characteristic sort of the crypto spot cross-section has beaten its same-coin control. The ridge control and a BTC-direction split were not reported. The long-horizon momentum claim is outside the sixty-day schema cap. One boom-and-bust window (K-0006). Low prior for more unless dated own-price events or BTC alone.

title: Perp crowding markers: no reproducible edge in six cards
statement: Six cards used leveraged-demand markers of liquid crypto perps: funding level (H-0039), funding change after crashes (H-0049), perp-versus-spot volume (H-0071), a US stress gate (H-0081), a learned momentum-by-basis score (H-0134) and, new, a slow own-history basis sort in half-year cohorts (H-0145). None cleared the same-coin placebo test with a bar under cost. H-0145 is a cannot-tell: right-signed with a negative placebo mean, so not coin identity, but the cloud was wide, the early third wrong-signed and the middle third carried the average. Open interest and liquidations remain unmeasured; the plain linear basis sort was never reported. Low prior for another crowding card on these perps without forced-flow data or a multi-cycle history.

title: A cut arbitrage link is not enough: single-company receipts did not revert during home closures, basket wrappers did
statement: K-0183 read wrapper deviations as reverting where creation and redemption cannot arbitrage them: country ETFs on home holidays (H-0133) and closed-end funds against an ETF anchor (K-0103). H-0157 applied the same cut link to single-company receipts of Asian companies during multi-day home closures. The unanchored excess move did not revert but continued, in every third and more at ten sessions than at three, on only a few dozen closure episodes (about one event date a year), so the sample is small and the sign is weak evidence. Reading, inferred and not tested: a basket wrapper has an anchor in its holdings that returns when the home market reopens, while a single-company receipt's move during the closure may carry company news that no home price contradicts. So what reverts is the flow part of a gap, not the information part, and a cut link is at most necessary. Which stocks the correlation rule assigned to home exchanges was never reported. A further wrapper card needs basket wrappers or many more closure dates, not single-company receipts.

title: Volatility risk premium: the cross-section of stocks by loading on volatility innovations is empty too
statement: K-0129 read the failed implied-over-realized rankings as inferred evidence that any premium is global and cancels in a relative sort, and left a time-series design as the only open route. H-0155 tested the cross-sectional form of the global premium directly: liquid stocks most hurt by VIX innovations, matched on beta and idiosyncratic volatility, held for months. Entries were right-signed in every third, but the same stocks on shifted dates earned far more, short horizons were negative and there was no build to a quarter, so the sort picks stocks that do well anyway and timing adds nothing. Beta was held fixed by cell, so the usual beta confound (K-0074) is an unlikely excuse; the placebo bar lay above cost but the event mean was below the placebo mean, so power was not the limit. The family now has five cards across stocks, ETFs and a volatility ETP. The loading was estimated from a noisy collinear regression; loadings from option prices are not loadable. A further card here has a low prior unless it is a time-series design across many markets with an always-invested control.

title: Session-VWAP setups on BTC/ETH five-minute perps: four directions, none pays at taker cost
statement: Four cards from one leaflet traded the UTC-session VWAP and its bands on BTC and ETH five-minute perps: continuation after acceptance outside the bands (H-0147), a fade of a rejected band-edge test (H-0148), the re-entry after a failed excursion (H-0149) and a held VWAP test continuing to the far band (H-0150). All died at G1 with negative net Sharpe, a bootstrap bound below zero and drawdown over the limit. Trade counts were large, several times the forecast for the two later setups: the faster clock buys events, not gross per event. Derived gross per trade (from mean net trade and cost share; not reported by the judge) was closest to cost for H-0147 and a small fraction of cost for the others. H-0149 and H-0150 take opposite sides of the same re-entries and both lost, so no direction is left to flip. With H-0137 to H-0142 and study 16 these are nine price-level taker rules on BTC and ETH with one fragile near pass (K-0194). Owner controls did not run (K-0193). Untested: maker execution, holds beyond a session.

title: Quarter-horizon stock sorts: nine designs, none beat the same-stock placebo, which takes most of the average
statement: Since K-0111, five more designs held liquid US stocks on a quarter-long label and ended at the mechanism test: asset growth by cash-flow discretion (H-0146), healthy cheap stocks (H-0151), large share-count jumps (H-0152), bond-proxy dividend stocks by rate state (H-0154) and aggregate-volatility loading (H-0155). With H-0054, H-0059, H-0083 and H-0086 that is nine, none passed: wrong-signed (H-0151); below the placebo mean (H-0154, H-0155, H-0086); mostly placebo identity (H-0146, H-0059); tiny in a wide cloud (H-0152); near misses with bars above cost (H-0054, H-0083). In the new cards the placebo mean was positive and about as large as the event mean: the sort picks stocks that earn on any date. Entry-only events remove that trap but widen the cloud (K-0111). Four of the five were long-only against raw peers (K-0074, K-0153). The three learned cards reported no ridge control and no split by state or side (K-0135). A further quarter-horizon stock sort has a low prior unless it reports the linear control and a beta-matched peer set.

title: Scout forecasts H-0146 to H-0157: calendar-key dates and confirmation-close counts wrong, gross below central
statement: Twelve cards. Event counts for slow stock sorts were in range or above (H-0146 forecast 3500-6500, counted about 14300; H-0154 forecast 3000-7000, counted 9296) and stock round trips matched (about 12 bps). Two kinds of count ran wrong.
